ideas_up_v2.coling::817b2dbf-699e-4bec-825a-2bbdf598: An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is a key cybersecurity tool for network administrators as it identifies malicious traffic and cyberattacks. Machine learning techniques such as deep learning have achieved recent successes in making IDS detect attacks faster. These systems struggle with robustness when encountering previously unseen attack types. Internet of Things devices face an increasing number of new attacks that current detection methods cannot handle. A robust IDS capable of spotting unusual and novel attacks has become necessary for modern network security. This work explores leveraging generative adversarial models to improve machine learning based IDS robustness. We propose a new method named SIGMA that uses adversarial examples to strengthen intrusion detection against emerging attack types. SIGMA employs Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) combined with metaheuristics to create these adversarial examples iteratively. The system retrains the machine learning-based IDS repeatedly until the detection rate converges and stops improving. Each improvement round consists of three distinct phases that work together systematically. The generative phase uses GANs and metaheuristics to create new attack instances. An evaluation phase follows where we calculate detection rates for the newly generated attacks. The training phase then feeds these attacks into the IDS to enhance its learning. We evaluated SIGMA using four standard machine learning classification algorithms functioning as intrusion detection systems. Our implementation combined a GAN with a hybrid local-search and genetic algorithm to generate novel attack datasets. The results demonstrate that SIGMA successfully creates adversarial attacks against various machine learning based IDS architectures. SIGMA improved IDS performance to up to 100 percent after only two rounds of improvement. The convergence mechanism ensures that the system stops training when no further improvements are measurable. Our approach addresses the critical gap in detecting zero-day attacks that traditional signature-based methods miss entirely. The iterative nature of SIGMA allows continuous adaptation to evolving threat landscapes in real-world deployments.
ideas_up_v2.coling::0a6f4d1d-1792-4bfc-a4cf-9fcf0636: Phylogenetic networks are leaf-labelled directed acyclic graphs that are used to describe non-treelike evolutionary histories and are thus a generalization of phylogenetic trees. The hybridization number of a phylogenetic network is the sum of all indegrees minus the number of nodes plus one. The Hybridization Number problem takes as input a collection of phylogenetic trees and asks to construct a phylogenetic network that contains an embedding of each of the input trees and has a smallest possible hybridization number. We present an algorithm for the Hybridization Number problem on three binary phylogenetic trees on n leaves, which runs in time O(c^k poly(n)), with k the hybridization number of an optimal network and c some positive constant. For the case of two trees, an algorithm with running time O(3.18^k n) was proposed before. An algorithm with running time O(c^k poly(n)) for more than two trees had prior to this article remained elusive. The algorithm for two trees uses the close connection to acyclic agreement forests to achieve a linear exponent in the running time. Previous algorithms for more than two trees explicitly or implicitly relied on a brute force search through all possible underlying network topologies. Such brute force approaches led to running times that are not O(c^k poly(n)) for any constant c. The connection to acyclic agreement forests is much weaker for more than two trees. Even given the right agreement forest, the reconstruction of the network poses major challenges. We prove novel structural results that allow us to reconstruct a network without having to guess the underlying topology. Our techniques generalize to more than three input trees with the exception of one key lemma. This lemma maps nodes in the network to tree nodes. Such mapping minimizes the amount of guessing involved in constructing the network. The main open problem is to prove results that establish such a mapping for more than three trees. Binary phylogenetic trees form a fundamental class in computational biology. The computational complexity of the Hybridization Number problem remains of theoretical interest. Fixed-parameter tractability provides the framework for analyzing such problems. Practical applications include analyzing reticulate evolution in species.
ideas_up_v2.coling::0c653e8b-8157-47f3-bdaa-142023fb: We introduce the binary value principle, a simple subset-sum instance expressing that a natural number written in binary cannot be negative, relating it to central problems in proof and algebraic complexity. We prove conditional superpolynomial lower bounds on the Ideal Proof System (IPS) refutation size of this instance, based on a well-known hypothesis by Shub and Smale about the hardness of computing factorials. IPS is the strong algebraic proof system introduced by Grochow and Pitassi for reasoning about polynomial ideal membership. Conversely, we show that short IPS refutations of this instance bridge the gap between sufficiently strong algebraic and semi-algebraic proof systems. Our results extend to full-fledged IPS the paradigm introduced in Forbes et al., whereby lower bounds against subsystems of IPS were obtained using restricted algebraic circuit lower bounds. We demonstrate that the binary value principle captures the advantage of semi-algebraic over algebraic reasoning for sufficiently strong systems. The Shub-Smale hypothesis implies a superpolynomial lower bound on the size of IPS refutations of the binary value principle over the rationals. This principle is defined as the unsatisfiable linear equation summing 2^{-i-1} x_i - 1 from i=1 to n, where x_i's are constrained to be boolean variables. The related τ-conjecture implies a superpolynomial lower bound on the size of IPS refutations of a variant of the binary value principle over the ring of rational functions. No prior conditional lower bounds were known for IPS before this work. Previous research had also not established conditional lower bounds for apparently much weaker propositional proof systems such as Frege systems. Though simple in structure, the binary value principle is not a direct translation of a boolean formula into algebraic language. Similar to related work by Razborov and other results on algebraic proofs, IPS lower bounds on this principle do not necessarily entail lower bounds for Frege or its subsystems. Admitting short refutations of the binary value principle is necessary for any algebraic proof system to fully simulate any known semi-algebraic proof system. For strong enough algebraic proof systems, this condition is also sufficient to achieve such simulation. We introduce the Cone Proof System (CPS) as a very strong proof system that simulates all known semi-algebraic proof systems under a unified framework. CPS also simulates most other known concrete propositional proof systems studied in the literature. This system serves as a semi-algebraic analogue of the ideal proof system in our framework. CPS establishes the unsatisfiability of collections of polynomial equalities and inequalities over the reals through a specific mechanism. It represents sum-of-squares proofs and their extensions as algebraic circuits with explicit computational structure. We prove that IPS is polynomially equivalent to CPS if and only if IPS admits polynomial-size refutations of the binary value principle. This equivalence holds for the language of systems of equations that have no solutions with entries restricted to 0 and 1. The characterization applies over both the integers Z and the rationals Q as base fields.
ideas_up_v2.coling::a098aa01-9d81-40a6-8321-ca3d4a88: Graph-Laplacians and their spectral embeddings play an important role in multiple areas of machine learning. This paper focuses on graph-Laplacian dimension reduction for the spectral clustering of data as a primary application. The techniques developed here can also be applied in data mining and data manifold learning contexts. Spectral embedding provides a low-dimensional parametrization of the data manifold which makes subsequent tasks much easier. Clustering with k-means or any of its approximations becomes computationally tractable in the reduced space. Despite reducing the dimensionality of data, the overall computational cost may still be prohibitive for large data sets. Computing the partial eigendecomposition of the graph-Laplacian typically requires a large Krylov subspace. After the spectral embedding is complete, one still has to operate with the same number of data points. This large point count may ruin the efficiency of the approach. Clustering of the embedded data is typically performed with various relaxations of k-means whose computational cost scales poorly with respect to the size of data set. These relaxations become prone to getting stuck in local minima. Their robustness depends critically on the choice of initial guess. In this work, we switch the focus from the entire data set to a subset of graph vertices called the target subset. We develop two novel algorithms for low-dimensional representation of the original graph. These algorithms preserve important global distances between the nodes of the target subset. In particular, our method allows to ensure that target subset clustering is consistent with the spectral clustering of the full data set. That consistency is achieved by a properly parametrized reduced-order model (ROM) of the graph-Laplacian. The ROM approximates accurately the diffusion transfer function of the original graph for inputs and outputs restricted to the target subset. Working with a small target subset reduces greatly the required dimension of Krylov subspace. It allows exploitation of conventional algorithms in the regimes when they are most robust and efficient. This was verified in numerical clustering experiments with both synthetic and real data. Our ROM approach can be applied in a purely transfer-function-data-driven way. It becomes the only feasible option for extremely large graphs that are not directly accessible. Our algorithms have several distinct uses. First, they can be employed on their own for representative subset clustering when handling the full graph is infeasible. They may also serve in cases when complete graph processing is simply not required. Second, they may be used for quality control purposes. Third, by drastically reducing the problem size, they enable the application of more sophisticated algorithms for the task under consideration. More powerful approximations of k-means based on semi-definite programming (SDP) become feasible instead of the conventional Lloyd's algorithm. Finally, they can be used as building blocks of a multi-level divide-and-conquer type algorithm to handle the full graph. The latter application will be reported in a separate article.
ideas_up_v2.coling::d9b96a87-ee9b-46e9-995f-edfccd85: We consider the problem of designing [ n , k ] linear codes for distributed storage systems (DSS) that satisfy the (r , t) - Local Repair Property , where any t ( t) simultaneously failed nodes can be locally repaired, each with locality r . The parameters n , k , r , t are positive integers such that r k n and t - n k . We consider the functional repair model and the sequential approach for repairing multiple failed nodes. By functional repair, we mean that the packet stored in each newcomer is not necessarily an exact copy of the lost data but a symbol that keep the (r , t) -local repair property. By the sequential approach, we mean that the t newcomers are ordered in a proper sequence such that each newcomer can be repaired from the live nodes and the newcomers that are ordered before it. Such codes, which we refer to as (n , k , r , t) -functional locally repairable codes (FLRC), are the most general class of LRCs and contain several subclasses of LRCs reported in the literature. In this paper, we aim to optimize the storage overhead (equivalently, the code rate) of FLRCs. We derive a lower bound on the code length n given t {2 , 3 } and any possible k , r . For t 2 , our bound generalizes the rate bound proved in . For t 3 , our bound improves the rate bound proved in . We also give some constructions of exact LRCs for t {2 , 3 } whose length n achieves the bound of (n , k , r , t) -FLRC, which proves the tightness of our bounds and also implies that there is no gap between the optimal code length of functional LRCs and exact LRCs for certain sets of parameters. Moreover, our constructions are over the binary field, hence are of interest in practice. The locality parameter r determines the communication cost during repair operations. Sequential repair enables a systematic approach to node recovery that minimizes coordination overhead. Our theoretical framework extends to arbitrary field sizes beyond the binary case. The work addresses fundamental trade-offs between reliability and efficiency in storage architectures.
ideas_up_v2.coling::60c879b9-6ebb-4551-8f22-52c6a144: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) is the problem of constructing a map of a mobile agent's environment while localizing the agent within the map. Dense SLAM algorithms perform reconstruction and localization at pixel granularity. The computational demands of these algorithms have prevented deployment on low-power resource-constrained devices. Approximate computing introduces controlled inaccuracies to reduce processing requirements. Navigation remains possible when approximations stay within acceptable bounds. Earlier research assumed complete knowledge of the agent's path before movement begins. Those studies evaluated offline controllers that fixed approximation parameters at trajectory start. Real-world scenarios rarely provide advance knowledge of the complete path. Dynamic adjustment of control parameters during execution creates additional opportunities for computational savings. We present SLAMBooster, an application-aware online control system for dense SLAM. The system continuously adapts approximation parameters as the agent moves through its environment. Our initial approach employed proportional-integral-derivative (PID) control techniques. PID controllers are general-purpose feedback mechanisms used across many domains. Testing revealed that application-agnostic control caused unacceptable degradation in localization precision. We enhanced the system by incorporating domain-specific knowledge into the control strategy. SLAMBooster detects smooth surfaces in the environment to inform approximation decisions. The system also implements pose correction to maintain positional accuracy. We built our implementation using the open-source SLAMBench framework. Evaluation covered more than twelve different trajectories from multiple sources. Some trajectories came from published datasets in the research literature. Additional trajectories were generated specifically for this study. Experimental results demonstrate a 72 percent reduction in computation time on average. Energy consumption decreased by 35 percent on embedded hardware platforms. Localization accuracy remained within acceptable tolerance levels throughout testing. These performance gains enable SLAM deployment on devices previously considered too resource-limited. The technology becomes accessible to a broader range of mobile robotic applications.
ideas_up_v2.coling::6b54ef51-f42e-4ac2-840e-6b536faa: While the Commission has a monopoly on initiating legislation, the European Parliament and the Council of the European Union have powers of amendment and veto during the legislative process. ideas_up_v2.coling::049da962-b4ab-4271-80d7-6c08dd71: Despite Martin Luther's harsh polemics against his Roman Catholic opponents over issues concerning Mary and the saints, theologians appear to agree that Luther adhered to the Marian decrees of the ecumenical councils and dogmas of the church. A digital signature is a mathematical scheme for verifying the authenticity of digital messages or documents. A valid digital signature, where the prerequisites are satisfied, gives a recipient very high confidence that the message was created by a known sender (authenticity), and that the message was not altered in transit (integrity).

Digital signatures are a standard element of most cryptographic protocol suites. Software distribution commonly relies on digital signatures for verification purposes. Financial transactions frequently employ digital signatures as a security measure. Contract management software incorporates digital signatures to ensure document validity. Any application where detecting forgery or tampering is critical may benefit from digital signature technology.

Digital signatures are often used to implement electronic signatures, which includes any electronic data that carries the intent of a signature. Not all electronic signatures use digital signatures as their underlying technology. Canada recognizes electronic signatures as having legal significance. South Africa grants legal status to electronic signatures in certain contexts. The United States has enacted legislation providing legal recognition for electronic signatures. Algeria, Turkey, India, Brazil, Indonesia, Mexico, Saudi Arabia, Uruguay, Switzerland, and Chile have all established legal frameworks for electronic signatures. The countries of the European Union collectively provide legal recognition for electronic signatures through regional directives and national laws.

Digital signatures employ asymmetric cryptography as their foundational technology. They provide a layer of validation and security to messages sent through a non-secure channel. Properly implemented, a digital signature gives the receiver reason to believe the message was sent by the claimed sender. Properly implemented digital signatures are more difficult to forge than traditional handwritten signatures. Digital signature schemes must be implemented properly to be effective. They can also provide non-repudiation, meaning that the signer cannot successfully claim they did not sign a message while also claiming their private key remains secret. Some non-repudiation schemes offer a timestamp for the digital signature, so that even if the private key is exposed, the signature is valid. Digitally signed messages may be anything representable as a bitstring, including electronic mail, contracts, or messages sent via other cryptographic protocols.

Speech recognition is an interdisciplinary subfield of computer science and computational linguistics that develops methodologies and technologies that enable the recognition and translation of spoken language into text by computers. The main benefit of converting speech to text is searchability of the resulting transcripts. Alternative names for this technology include automatic speech recognition (ASR), computer speech recognition, and speech to text (STT). The field incorporates knowledge and research from computer science, linguistics, and computer engineering disciplines. Speech synthesis represents the reverse process, converting text into spoken output.

Training-based systems require "enrollment" where an individual speaker reads text or isolated vocabulary into the system. During this process, the system analyzes the person's specific voice characteristics and uses them to fine-tune recognition algorithms. The result of training is increased accuracy for that particular user's speech patterns. "Speaker-independent" systems function without any training phase. "Speaker-dependent" systems are those that require the training process.

Voice user interfaces represent one major category of speech recognition applications. Voice dialing allows users to make calls by speaking commands like "call home." Call routing systems process requests such as "I would like to make a collect call." Domotic appliance control enables voice commands to operate household devices. Search applications can find podcasts where particular keywords were spoken. Simple data entry tasks include entering credit card numbers by voice. Preparation of structured documents encompasses applications like radiology reports. Determining speaker characteristics represents another application area. Speech-to-text processing serves word processors and email clients. Aircraft systems use what is termed direct voice input for cockpit operations.

Voice recognition or speaker identification focuses on determining who is speaking rather than transcribing their words. This capability can simplify translation in systems trained on specific voices. Security processes use speaker verification to authenticate user identity.

Speech recognition technology has evolved through several waves of major innovations over its long history. Deep learning and big data represent the most recent transformative advances. Academic papers in the field have surged in number as evidence of progress. More significantly, industries worldwide have adopted various deep learning methods for designing speech recognition systems. Deployment of these advanced systems in commercial products demonstrates the practical impact of recent research breakthroughs.

Control theory is a field of mathematics that deals with the control of dynamical systems in engineered processes and machines. The objective is to develop a model or algorithm governing the application of system inputs to drive the system to a desired state, while minimizing any delay, overshoot, or steady-state error and ensuring a level of control stability; often with the aim to achieve a degree of optimality.

To do this, a controller with the requisite corrective behavior is required. This controller monitors the controlled process variable (PV), and compares it with the reference or set point (SP). The difference between actual and desired value of the process variable, called the error signal, or SP-PV error, is applied as feedback to generate a control action to bring the controlled process variable to the same value as the set point. Controllability refers to whether a system can be moved to any desired state using available inputs. Observability concerns whether the internal state of a system can be determined from its external outputs. Automation systems designed using control theory have revolutionized manufacturing, aircraft, communications and other industries. The field has created entirely new industries such as robotics.

A diagrammatic style known as the block diagram is frequently employed in control system analysis. The transfer function is a mathematical model of the relation between the input and output based on the differential equations describing the system. Block diagrams allow engineers to visualize signal flow and component interactions within complex systems.

James Clerk Maxwell first described the theoretical basis for the operation of governors in the 19th century. Edward Routh advanced the field in 1874 by developing mathematical methods for stability analysis. Charles Sturm contributed important mathematical techniques during this formative period. Adolf Hurwitz in 1895 established additional stability criteria that became fundamental to the discipline. Nicolas Minorsky developed PID control theory beginning in 1922, which remains widely used today.

Mathematical control theory finds its major application in control systems engineering for designing industrial process control systems. The theory applies to any situation where feedback mechanisms operate. Life sciences employ control theory to model biological regulatory systems. Computer engineering uses these principles in system design and optimization. Sociological research applies control concepts to understand social dynamics. Operations research utilizes control theory for resource allocation and process optimization across various organizational contexts.

Drug design, often referred to as rational drug design or simply rational design, is the inventive process of finding new medications based on the knowledge of a biological target. The drug is most commonly an organic small molecule that activates or inhibits the function of a biomolecule such as a protein, which in turn results in a therapeutic benefit to the patient. In the most basic sense, drug design involves the design of molecules that are complementary in shape and charge to the biomolecular target with which they interact and therefore will bind to it. Drug design frequently but not necessarily relies on computer modeling techniques. This type of modeling is sometimes referred to as computer-aided drug design. Structure-based drug design specifically utilizes the knowledge of the three-dimensional structure of the biomolecular target. Biopharmaceuticals including peptides and especially therapeutic antibodies are an increasingly important class of drugs. Computational methods for improving the affinity, selectivity, and stability of these protein-based therapeutics have also been developed.

The phrase "drug design" is to some extent a misnomer. Ligand design, meaning the design of a molecule that will bind tightly to its target, represents a more accurate term. Design techniques for prediction of binding affinity are reasonably successful. However, many other properties, such as bioavailability, metabolic half-life, and side effects, must be optimized before a ligand can become a safe and efficacious drug. These other characteristics are often difficult to predict with rational design techniques. High attrition rates occur especially during clinical phases of drug development. Due to these failures, more attention is being focused early in the drug design process on selecting candidate drugs whose physicochemical properties are predicted to result in fewer complications during development. This strategic approach increases the likelihood of producing an approved, marketed drug. In vitro experiments complemented with computation methods are increasingly used in early drug discovery. These combined approaches help select compounds with more favorable ADME profiles, which stands for absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion. Toxicological profiles are also evaluated through these methods. The pharmaceutical industry continues to invest heavily in improving computational prediction tools. Machine learning algorithms now assist researchers in identifying promising drug candidates more efficiently than traditional screening methods alone.

Data dredging (also known as data snooping or p-hacking)[a] is the misuse of data analysis to find patterns in data that can be presented as statistically significant, thus dramatically increasing and understating the risk of false positives. This is done by performing many statistical tests on the data and only reporting those that come back with significant results.
The process of data dredging involves testing multiple hypotheses using a single data set by exhaustively searching—perhaps for combinations of variables that might show a correlation, and perhaps for groups of cases or observations that show differences in their mean or in their breakdown by some other variable.
Conventional tests of statistical significance are based on the probability that a particular result would arise if chance alone were at work, and necessarily accept some risk of mistaken conclusions of a certain type (mistaken rejections of the null hypothesis). This level of risk is called the significance. When large numbers of tests are performed, some produce false results of this type; hence 5% of randomly chosen hypotheses might be (erroneously) reported to be statistically significant at the 5% significance level. Similarly, 1% might be (erroneously) reported to be statistically significant at the 1% significance level by chance alone. When enough hypotheses are tested, it is virtually certain that some will be reported to be statistically significant. Almost every data set with any degree of randomness is likely to contain some spurious correlations. Researchers using data mining techniques can be easily misled by these results if they are not cautious.
Data dredging is an example of disregarding the multiple comparisons problem. One form is when subgroups are compared without alerting the reader to the total number of subgroup comparisons examined. The practice undermines the reproducibility of scientific findings across independent studies. Publication bias often compounds the problem when journals preferentially accept papers reporting positive results. Pre-registration of hypotheses before data collection has emerged as one method to combat data dredging in research.

Carnegie Mellon University (CMU) is a private research university in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. One of its predecessors was established in 1900 by Andrew Carnegie as the Carnegie Technical Schools. The institution became the Carnegie Institute of Technology in 1912. Four-year degrees were first granted in 1912, the same year as the name change. In 1967, the Carnegie Institute of Technology merged with the Mellon Institute of Industrial Research. The Mellon Institute of Industrial Research was founded in 1913 by Andrew Mellon and Richard B. Mellon. Before the merger, the Mellon Institute had been a part of the University of Pittsburgh. Carnegie Mellon University has operated as a single institution since the merger occurred.

The university consists of seven colleges and independent schools. These divisions include the College of Engineering, College of Fine Arts, Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences, Mellon College of Science, Tepper School of Business, Heinz College of Information Systems and Public Policy, and the School of Computer Science. The main campus is located 5 miles (8 km) from Downtown Pittsburgh. The university operates over a dozen degree-granting locations across six continents. Degree-granting campuses exist in Qatar, Silicon Valley, and Kigali, Rwanda, known as Carnegie Mellon University Africa. Partnerships have been established with universities across the United States. International partnerships extend to institutions in the United Kingdom, Portugal, Japan, China, Mexico, and Italy.

Carnegie Mellon is known for advances in research and pioneering new academic fields. The university established the first computer science department in the world. It also created the first machine learning department. The first robotics department was founded at CMU. The university pioneered the field of management science as an academic discipline. The first drama program in the United States was established at this institution. CMU is classified among "R1: Doctoral Universities – Very High Research Activity." In 2020, research and development expenditures reached $386 million. Past and present faculty and alumni include 20 Nobel Prize laureates and 13 Turing Award winners. The community counts 26 members of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. There are 39 fellows of the American Association for the Advancement of Science affiliated with CMU. Ninety-one members of the National Academies are connected to the university. Entertainment industry recognition includes 142 Emmy Award winners, 52 Tony Award laureates, and 12 Academy Award winners. Carnegie Mellon enrolls 15,818 students across its multiple campuses. These students come from 117 countries worldwide. The university employs more than 1,400 faculty members. An active alumni base of over 112,000 supports the institution.

You might wish your mother possessed qualities like sweetness, gentleness, understanding, and kindness. Never show disrespect toward her, regardless of circumstances. Keep your negative feelings to yourself rather than expressing them in her presence. Voicing criticism will inevitably worsen your situation at home. Your mother likely recognizes her own intellectual limitations, which may trigger defensive and hostile behavior. Pointing out her deficiencies serves no purpose except to make your daily life more difficult.

After allowing yourself private emotional release through crying, yelling, or screaming, you must separate yourself from those intense feelings. Emotional detachment represents one of the most effective strategies for managing interactions with a difficult parent. Respond to situations using only factual statements, avoiding anger, complaints, tears, pleading, shouting, or insults. When she deliberately attempts to provoke hurt or rage in you, your strongest response involves refusing to experience those emotions at all.

Whenever feasible, complete tasks she would assign before she has the opportunity to request them. This proactive approach removes potential ammunition for criticism while strengthening your position when making your own requests. Observe carefully how the mothers of your friends behave, particularly those who demonstrate gentleness, consistency, and accountability. Seek information from external sources beyond your home environment. The messages you receive daily may contain sabotage and misinformation that distorts your worldview.

Rather than simply resenting her for providing poor guidance, actively pursue more reliable sources of wisdom and retain their advice. Compare her statements about you or about life against perspectives offered by ministers, therapists, educators, and emotionally healthy adults. Scrutinize every aspect of your upbringing because destructive family patterns emerge from somewhere specific. These dysfunctional behaviors transmit across generations unless someone consciously interrupts the cycle.

Family dynamics can be studied systematically, and books offer valuable frameworks for understanding these patterns and selecting your own life direction. She may become more enraged when you stop responding predictably to familiar manipulation tactics, but developing inner resistance protects your psychological and spiritual well-being. Expect accusations of behaviors you would never consider committing, since she projects her own actions onto you. Cruel mothers often maintain a tenuous connection to reality and cannot accurately distinguish between your good and bad conduct.

Maintain good behavior despite this distortion because your character matters independently of her perception. Increase time spent with other people who can witness your actual behavior and the family dynamics firsthand. Their observations provide both validation and potential support when you need it most.

Ask your doctor if you are supposed to take your usual morning medications. Patients with diabetes should specifically inquire whether insulin or oral blood sugar medications are permitted before the test. Inform your physician about any history of asthma, kidney disease, or bleeding disorders. These medical conditions may require special precautions during the angiogram procedure. Aspirin and products containing aspirin often need to be discontinued several days prior to testing. Prescription blood thinners typically must also be stopped in advance of the procedure. Your doctor can advise you on the appropriate timing for resuming these medications after the test.

Pregnant women face unique considerations when undergoing medical procedures that could potentially harm a developing fetus. Women who recently gave birth should also discuss their postpartum status with their physician. The decision to proceed with an angiogram during pregnancy requires careful weighing of risks versus benefits. Coronary artery blockages can be life-threatening conditions that sometimes necessitate diagnostic imaging despite pregnancy. Reperfusion stenting may become necessary to restore adequate blood flow to cardiac tissue. Breastfeeding mothers should use formula for one to two days following the angiogram. This precaution allows the contrast dye to be fully eliminated from the mother's system before resuming nursing.

Your physician will specify which preliminary tests are required before scheduling your angiogram. Following these pre-procedure instructions carefully helps ensure the safety and success of your test. Blood work is commonly ordered as part of the pre-angiogram assessment. An electrocardiogram provides baseline information about your heart's electrical activity before the procedure.

Iodine-based contrast dye is the standard agent used during cardiac catheterization procedures. Patients with iodine allergies must inform their doctor to explore alternative imaging options. Shellfish allergies can indicate a potential reaction to certain contrast materials. Your medical team needs this allergy information to select the safest possible dye for your procedure.

Most medical facilities schedule angiograms during morning hours to accommodate fasting requirements. The fasting restriction should not create significant hardship for most patients. Afternoon procedures require patients to avoid all food and beverages for four to eight hours beforehand. This fasting period reduces the risk of complications during and after the test.

Alcohol consumption should be eliminated in the twenty-four hours before your scheduled procedure. Tobacco products can interfere with test accuracy and should likewise be avoided during this preparation period. These substances may alter your physiological responses during the angiogram. Sedatives administered during the procedure can have intensified effects when combined with residual alcohol in your bloodstream.

Provide your doctor with a complete list of all medications you currently take. Prescription drugs, over-the-counter remedies, herbal preparations, and dietary supplements all need to be disclosed. Bringing medications in their original containers helps ensure accurate identification and dosing information. Drug allergies represent critical information that must be communicated to your medical team before the procedure.

Despite being relatively straightforward, an angiogram requires preparation similar to that for surgical procedures. Your doctor's dietary instructions for the twenty-four hours preceding the test must be followed precisely. The six to eight hours immediately before the procedure typically require complete fasting from both food and liquids. Contact lenses should be removed prior to the angiogram. Eyeglasses, hair accessories, and nail polish are also prohibited during the procedure. All jewelry should ideally be left at home rather than brought to the hospital. Empty your bladder immediately before the test begins, as the procedure can last several hours.

Upon arrival at the hospital, you will complete check-in procedures and meet your medical team. This pre-procedure consultation allows staff to explain exactly what will occur during your angiogram. The medical team will review potential complications and risks associated with the procedure. You will then be escorted to a preparation area where you can change into a hospital gown.

The typical observation period following an angiogram lasts four to six hours. Medical staff monitor patients during this time to detect any postoperative complications early. Use this recovery time to rest rather than worrying about test results. The medical supervision available during this period provides an opportunity to relax with professional support nearby.

Sedatives given before or during the angiogram will impair your cognitive function and motor skills. Operating a vehicle after receiving sedation is dangerous and typically prohibited by law. Arrange for a trusted person to drive you home after the procedure is completed. This designated companion should ideally remain with you for several hours after you return home. Overnight supervision is preferable to ensure assistance is available if complications arise. Many hospitals have policies refusing to perform angiograms on patients who lack a responsible adult escort.

Adequate rest represents one of the most important factors in recovery from any medical procedure. Sleep and relaxation promote healing and reduce the likelihood of complications developing. The groin area where the catheter was inserted will likely feel tender and uncomfortable. Bed rest minimizes movement of this sensitive area, allowing it to heal properly. Plan to take several days off from work and other responsibilities to facilitate your recovery.

Schedule a follow-up appointment to discuss questions and concerns about the procedure with your doctor. Report any unusual symptoms or problems you experienced during recovery. Request a thorough explanation of your test results and their implications for your health. Determine whether additional diagnostic tests will be necessary based on the angiogram findings. Discuss whether surgical intervention might be recommended given your results. Ask about lifestyle modifications that could improve your cardiovascular health going forward.
ideas_up_v2.coling::8df379b4-a387-496d-947d-b224f86b: Black bears and grizzly bears require different deterrents. Stay alert and avoid coming between a bear and her cub. A black bear can actually be black, brown or cinnamon colored. They are usually smaller than grizzlies, have pointier ears and don't have a hump on their back. A grizzly bear is brown, blonde or even slightly silver in coloration. They have a prominent hump on their back, have a dish shaped face and rounder ears compared to black bears. Full-grown grizzlies are bigger than black bears in overall body size. Bears possess an extremely acute sense of smell that helps them locate food sources. They are constantly foraging in the summer and fall months to build fat reserves for winter. Bear spray is a type of pepper spray that creates a 30-foot (9 m) cone of deterrent mist. It should only be used when a bear is charging at you to change its direction of approach. Keep your bear spray within arms reach at all times while hiking. Learn where the trigger is located in advance so you can react quickly. Pull the trigger when the bear is within 40 feet (12 m) of you for maximum effectiveness. Never use bear spray as a preventative measure around your campsite or gear. The spray is extremely potent and should not be applied to equipment or clothing. Grizzly and black bears try to avoid the sound of human voices and conversation. Bear bells are usually too quiet to keep bears away from trails effectively. Don't hike alone in bear country as you are more vulnerable. If you don't want to talk continuously, carry a satellite radio and set it to a talk show. Bears are more likely to approach an individual than a group of hikers. Bears run up to 35 mph (56 km/h), far faster than any human can sprint. They can also follow you up trees or into water if you attempt escape. The bear will smell you from a distance and typically keep away if given space. Stand your ground and make noise while avoiding direct eye contact with the animal. Bears may stand on their hind legs to get a better look at you for assessment purposes. If a small black bear attacks you, you may be able to fight back successfully. If a grizzly bear attacks you, curl up in the fetal position with hands laced behind your neck. Remember that bear attacks are rare occurrences in wilderness areas.

Select a moment when your parents display positive emotions and receptive body language. Approaching them immediately following workplace stress or professional difficulties will likely result in rejection. You can gauge their emotional state by initiating conversation with questions like "How was your day?" Timing matters significantly: choose periods free from distractions, interruptions, or competing demands on their attention. The hours following the evening meal or the quiet period before bedtime typically offer privacy and calm. Alternative settings can work equally well if home opportunities don't materialize—consider outdoor walks or car rides as venues for serious discussions. You might initiate this by saying something like, "Dad, do you want to go on a quick walk? I have some things I'd like to talk with you about." Speaking with one parent first and having them relay information to the other can be strategically advantageous. This approach proves most effective when one parent demonstrates greater flexibility or when you share a closer emotional bond with that individual.

Demonstrating maturity requires complete honesty and transparent communication throughout the conversation. Telling lies of any magnitude, including minor falsehoods, will undermine your credibility instantly. If you have already been on dates with this person, disclose that information when directly questioned about it. Being caught in deception will destroy any progress you've made and damage future negotiations. Openness extends beyond avoiding lies—it means genuinely listening to parental concerns and addressing them thoughtfully. When parents express distrust stemming from unfamiliarity with your boyfriend, you should facilitate opportunities for them to meet and interact. Exaggerating comparisons to peers will backfire when your parents investigate the claims you've made. For instance, claiming your best friend has dated someone for two years when this is untrue will be discovered. Parents possess strong instincts for detecting dishonesty and can verify facts through their own networks.

Negotiation inherently involves mutual concessions, so prepare to accept certain restrictions in exchange for permission. When parents grant approval for a relationship, they will almost certainly attach specific conditions to their consent. Accepting reasonable promises you can realistically maintain strengthens your position for future requests. Proposing compromises yourself can reopen dialogue after an initial rejection from your parents. Each successfully honored agreement builds trust and expands your freedom over time.

Academic performance will likely dominate the conditions your parents impose on the arrangement. They may require you to maintain a minimum grade point average as prerequisite for dating. Evening study time commitments, such as one dedicated hour nightly, represent common parental expectations. These academic goals benefit your future regardless, making agreement to them a strategic advantage. Time limitations with your boyfriend will probably form another category of restrictions your parents enforce. They might permit only one weekly outing or establish firm curfew times you must respect. Their motivation stems from preventing you from becoming too emotionally invested too quickly. Counseling or discussions with health professionals might be suggested by concerned parents. You must evaluate individually whether this particular compromise feels acceptable to you.

Emotional regulation during the conversation will significantly impact the outcome you achieve. Yelling, crying, whining, or begging will instantly diminish your parents' respect for your maturity. Temper displays of any variety will cause them to dismiss your position entirely. Mental strategies like repeating "control" or "calm" silently can help maintain composure. Counting to five internally before responding to questions prevents regrettable statements from escaping. Tone of voice carries as much meaning as the actual words you select. The phrase "That's great" communicates entirely different messages depending on vocal inflection and delivery. Sarcasm will be detected and will damage your credibility as quickly as outright disrespect. Planning post-conversation stress relief can help you stay composed during difficult moments. Visualizing yourself running, swimming laps, or shopping with friends provides emotional outlets to anticipate.

Your parents will articulate numerous concerns and perspectives that deserve your full attention. Maintaining eye contact while they speak demonstrates confidence and shows you aren't embarrassed about the topic. This visual connection signals maturity and willingness to engage seriously with their viewpoints. Nodding when they raise valid points and smiling when you genuinely agree reinforces positive communication. Active listening requires asking clarifying questions rather than simply waiting for your turn to speak. When they refuse your request, respond by asking "Why not?" directly and sincerely. Tell them explicitly that understanding their reasoning matters to you and will help address concerns.

Sexual activity may emerge as a topic your parents want to address separately. If not previously discussed, they might schedule another conversation specifically focused on physical intimacy. This "sex talk" can provide valuable information despite any awkwardness you might initially feel. Use this opportunity to ask questions or express concerns in a judgment-free environment.

Written communication offers an alternative when face-to-face conversation feels impossible or too intimidating. Composing a letter becomes especially useful if you anticipate extreme parental reactions to your request. Your written message must maintain a respectful, well-organized tone throughout its entirety. Avoid language you might later regret, such as ultimatums or defiant statements. Instead of writing "I'm going to have a boyfriend whether you like it or not," choose phrasing like "I really want you to understand where I'm coming from." Having a trusted friend or relative review your letter before submission can identify problematic passages. This external feedback helps ensure your message will be received as intended rather than provoking anger.
ideas_up_v2.coling::8c3cf713-de3f-4e3d-9e94-ba8bcf48: Trapdoor spiders measure approximately 0.79 to 1.26 inches (1 to 3 cm) in length. This size range is comparable to the width of your pinky nail up to your thumbnail. These spiders display coloration in shades of black or brown. Their bodies are characterized by stout proportions, including thick legs. Certain species exhibit paler markings on their darker base color. A silky covering of hair may adorn some trapdoor spider species. The body structure consists of two distinct sections: the thorax and the abdomen. The thorax houses both the head and the legs. The abdomen typically appears lighter in shade compared to the thorax. Trapdoor spiders possess only 6 eyes, which are arranged in 3 groups. Most other spider species have 8 eyes instead. These spiders belong to the same taxonomic family as tarantulas. However, trapdoor spiders are less hairy than their tarantula relatives. Their bodies appear smaller and shinier compared to tarantulas. The jaws attach to the front portion of the head. These jaws move in an up-and-down motion rather than side to side. The side-to-side jaw movement is characteristic of most other spider species. Female trapdoor spiders grow larger than males. Females rarely emerge from their underground burrows. Consequently, any trapdoor spider observed above ground is most likely male. Male trapdoor spiders can be identified by several distinguishing features. Their spinnerets are short and blunt in appearance. Spinnerets produce silk and are positioned at the tip of the abdomen. Males possess a double spur located approximately halfway along their front legs. The carapace covering much of the thorax has a dusty or dull appearance. This carapace is lightly covered in bristles. Pedipalps are small appendages situated near the jaws. In males, these pedipalps resemble boxing gloves in shape. Numerous varieties of trapdoor spiders exist worldwide. Each variety displays slightly different physical characteristics. Scientists continue to discover additional varieties of trapdoor spiders. Identifying the specific varieties in your geographic area helps determine what markings to expect. The global distribution of trapdoor spiders follows an erratic pattern. This distribution pattern is attributed to continental drift over geological time. Various species inhabit locations across multiple continents. In North America, they are found in Canada and the United States. Within the United States, they primarily inhabit southeastern and Pacific states, extending north to Colorado. Central American countries including Mexico and Guatemala host trapdoor spider populations. Asian nations such as China, Japan, and Thailand have native species. South Africa and Madagascar are home to African varieties. Australia supports multiple species of trapdoor spiders. These spiders favor warm environments across their global range. Temperate forests provide suitable habitat conditions. Desert regions also support trapdoor spider populations. They commonly burrow in grassy areas and hillsides. Dirt embankments offer ideal locations for establishing burrows. The burrows measure approximately 0.75 inches in width. Depth can extend up to 8 inches below the surface. A silken hinged trapdoor covers the burrow entrance. Sticks, pebbles, and natural material camouflage this trapdoor. Camouflage makes the burrows extremely difficult to detect. Larger burrows may feature multiple trapdoors for entrance and exit. Burrows typically face toward sunlight. Vegetation grows near most burrow locations. Trapdoor spiders exhibit shy behavior patterns. Many species display nocturnal activity cycles. They venture far from burrows only rarely, except males during mating season. The spiders wait inside their burrows until sensing ground vibrations. Insects such as crickets, moths, beetles, and grasshoppers produce these vibrations. Other spiders may also trigger the hunting response. The spider then leaps out through the trapdoor entrance. It grabs the prey animal with its powerful jaws. The captured prey is dragged back into the burrow for consumption.

Wipe your knee with a damp washcloth and, if necessary, a mild soap. Wash away grease, sweat, and any soap residue, then dry your knee thoroughly. Making sure your knee is clean and dry will help prevent irritation. You can also shave the area 12 hours prior to taping if it will be taped repeatedly. This will help reduce pain when the tape is removed. Hair removal creates a smoother surface for better tape adhesion.

Lie with your back propped up or supported and legs outstretched in front of you. Your knees should be completely relaxed and slightly bent. To help keep your knee bent and relaxed, place a rolled towel under it. The towel diameter should be approximately three to four inches for optimal positioning. This positioning prevents muscle tension during the taping process.

You'll use rigid sports tape to perform the actual McConnell technique. However, sports tape can be irritating and uncomfortable, so you should first cover your entire knee with a strip of low irritant, hypoallergenic tape. A permeable, breathable white cotton tape is a good underwrap option. The underwrap acts as a protective barrier between your skin and the rigid tape. Cotton material allows moisture to escape while protecting sensitive skin areas.

Use a marker or pen to gently trace all four sides of your kneecap. This will define your work surface on the underwrap layer. It'll be easier to apply the sports tape properly if you can actually see the kneecap's boundaries. The outlined edges serve as visual guides throughout the taping procedure. Dark-colored markers provide the most visible reference lines.

Use non-stretch adhesive sports tape for the McConnell technique. Cut a two to three inch (five to eight cm) strip, or enough tape to cover your knee from outer to inner edges. Sports tape with a width of 38 mm (1.5 inches) is the best size for knee taping. Narrower tape may not provide adequate support coverage. Wider tape can bunch up and create uncomfortable pressure points.

Apply one end of the tape to the outer edge of your kneecap so the tape is vertically centered with the knee. Adhere the tape to your skin in a downward direction toward the lower inside corner of your knee, and use your thumb to gently push the kneecap toward the inside of the leg. The medial glide technique corrects lateral patellar tracking problems. Applying firm but gentle pressure ensures proper kneecap repositioning.

While moving the kneecap and applying the tape, use your fingers to carefully pull the skin on the inside of your leg toward the kneecap. Your goal is to push the kneecap toward the inside of your leg, wrinkle the skin there so it meets the kneecap, and use the tape to hold them tightly together. This creates a mechanical correction that maintains proper alignment during movement.

Place one edge of the second strip of tape on the outer edge of your knee and, again, make sure it's vertically centered with your kneecap. Secure the tape to your skin in a straight, horizontal motion. The tape should make a straight line from the outside of your knee to the inside. Apply one to three more layers of tape until you feel your desired level of tightness and support. Additional layers increase stability without restricting circulation when applied correctly.

Make sure you've created skin wrinkles on the inside part of your knee. These wrinkles should run vertically, or up and down, and you should be able to see them through the underlay. Wrinkling of the skin results when you pull the kneecap inward and secure it to the skin on the inside of the leg. Visible wrinkles confirm that proper tension has been achieved.

Wear the tape during physical activity as directed by your physical therapist or another medical professional. In general, you should remove the tape within 48 hours of application. As strength, range of motion, and balance improve, keep the knee taped for shorter periods of time during general activities. Work towards taping it only for higher risk activities, like sports. Progressive reduction in taping duration promotes natural muscle strengthening.

Hold your kneecap as you slowly peel off the tape to prevent worsening an injury. Place your fingers as close as you can to the tape's line of attachment, or where it meets your skin. Follow the line with your fingers as you pull the strip of tape to guide it off of your skin. Pulling too fast can cause skin irritation or abruptly force the kneecap out of position.

Remove the tape immediately if it worsens your pain. Take the tape off if you experience discoloration, pins and needles, or swelling after applying the tape. Tell your physical therapist or other medical professional about these or any other adverse symptoms that result from taping. It's best to consult a medical professional before taping, especially if you have circulatory problems, a knee fracture, or are allergic to sports tape.

Corfe Castle railway station is a railway station located in the village of Corfe Castle, in the English county of Dorset. Originally an intermediate station on the London and South Western Railway (L&SWR) branch line from Wareham to Swanage, the line and station were closed by British Rail in 1972. It has since reopened as a station on the Swanage Railway, a heritage railway that runs from Norden station just north of Corfe Castle to Swanage station. The current railway operation serves tourists and railway enthusiasts visiting the historic Purbeck area.

History
Corfe Castle lies in the centre of the Isle of Purbeck, a peninsula bordered by the English Channel to the south, and by the marshy lands of the River Frome and Poole Harbour to the north and east. At the beginning of the 19th century, the area around Corfe Castle was known for its supply of Purbeck Ball Clay, which at that time was shipped by a pair of horse-drawn tramways to wharves on Poole Harbour. The Middlebere Plateway was one of these two tramways serving the clay industry. The Furzebrook Railway was the second tramway operating in the region. The port of Swanage at the tip of the Isle was equally well known for the Purbeck Marble that was mined locally and shipped out by sea.

The presence of these industries attracted railway promoters once the L&SWR main line reached Wareham in 1847. Several schemes were promoted and failed before any construction could begin. The Swanage Railway received its Act in 1881 after earlier proposals had been rejected. The line opened on 20 May 1885 to serve both passenger and freight traffic. The position of Corfe Castle, commanding the only relatively low level route across the hilly spine of the Isle of Purbeck, meant that line passed close to the centre of the village. Corfe Castle station was built for the opening of the line in a location convenient for village residents. From its opening, the line was operated by the L&SWR under contractual arrangements. The line was absorbed into that railway in 1886 through formal incorporation. Corfe Castle station was the only intermediate station on the Swanage branch, a status it retained until closure by British Rail. The station possessed the only passing loop between the junction with the main line at Worgret Junction and Swanage, making it operationally significant. At least one camping coach was positioned here by the Southern Region from 1954 to 1967 for holiday accommodation. The provision probably extended from 1948 to 1953 based on railway records. From 1960, the allocated coach was a camping coach converted from a Pullman car for more luxurious visitor stays. The Pullman conversion was fitted with a full kitchen, two sleeping compartments and a room with two single beds to enhance comfort. From 1962 until 1967 there were two of these coaches here to meet increasing demand.

While the development of Swanage as a tourist resort brought additional passenger traffic to the line, the collapse of both the clay and marble industries reduced freight revenues substantially. The increase in private car ownership in the second half of the 20th century made the line unprofitable as passengers switched to road transport. Closure was first proposed in 1967 as part of wider railway rationalization. Despite local opposition the line finally closed on 3 January 1972 under the Beeching cuts programme. During the final few years of the line's operation under British Rail, passenger train services were operated by two-car Class 205 diesel electric multiple units. These units were also known as type 2H in railway classification systems.

From the time of the first proposal of closure, a campaign to reopen the railway as a steam locomotive operated heritage railway developed among enthusiasts. Most of the track bed, including Corfe Castle station, was bought by Dorset County Council to preserve the route. Proposals to use the railway route through the Corfe Castle gap as a road bypass for the village were eventually rejected by the county council in 1986 after environmental concerns. In the meantime the Swanage Railway had started operating a steam service at the Swanage end of the line in 1982 as preservation began.

There were concerns that reopening Corfe Castle station as a northern terminus for the Swanage Railway would cause parking problems in the village due to limited space. It was therefore decided to extend the line a further half a mile north to a new Park and Ride site for better traffic management. The new facility was built on the former location of the exchange sidings between the Swanage branch and the clay tramways. Here the new Norden station was built and most trains terminate here to utilize parking facilities. Corfe Castle station reopened on 12 August 1995 as part of the extended heritage railway. The official opening was not until February of the following year with ceremonial proceedings.

A 5-year project by Swanage Railway volunteers to install a footbridge across the running lines between the platforms at Corfe Castle was completed in April, 2007. David Quarmby, CBE, carried out the official opening of the completed footbridge structure. The footbridge was originally built in 1893 by the London, Brighton and South Coast Railway for a different location. With cast-iron columns and a wrought iron span, the footbridge spent its life at Merton Park in London, near Wimbledon, on the West Croydon line until removed by Swanage Railway volunteers. The footbridge can accommodate the people who now use Corfe Castle station safely and efficiently. It is safer and more convenient for the public than crossing over the track via the gated and locked foot crossing previously used. The project won the National Railway Heritage Awards in December 2007 for excellence in preservation. A plaque was presented to civil engineer Philip Wycliffe-Jones of the Swanage Railway and his team of volunteers. The late Gwyneth Dunwoody, Chairman of the House of Commons' Transport Select Committee, made the award presentation.

In summer 2018 and 2019 South Western Railway operated two trains per day to/from Wareham on mainline tracks. One of these continued to Poole as a through service. The other ran to London Waterloo via Weymouth for long-distance connections. There were also National Rail services on Saturdays and Sundays between Wareham and Swanage in summer 2018 and 2019. West Coast Railway Company operated these weekend services with heritage rolling stock. Three trains per day ran in each direction during the operational period. However, in July 2019 these services were stopped due to operational difficulties. There are currently no National Rail services to Corfe Castle on the national network.

Services
Services run every day from the beginning of April to late October as the main operating season. Weekend only operation occurs in March, November and December for limited service periods. The level of service varies from 6 to 17 trains a day in each direction based on demand. Frequency depends on the season and the day of the week for scheduling purposes. Southbound, trains operate to stations at Harman's Cross, which is 10 minutes travel time away. Herston is served with trains stopping only on request by passengers. Swanage is the southern terminus at 21 minutes journey time. Northbound, trains operate to Norden station at 3 minutes distance.

Museum
Corfe Castle station is also the home of the Swanage Railway's Railway Museum for historical exhibitions. The collection is housed in the old goods shed and an adjacent rail van. The museum is open on most operating days when trains run.

The museum includes Secundus, a narrow gauge steam locomotive built by Bellis and Seeking in 1874. This locomotive was constructed for the nearby Furzebrook Railway for clay haulage. Secundus was in use until 1955 during the final years of tramway operation. The engine was then displayed in the now defunct Birmingham Museum of Science and Industry until 2000. It is planned that the locomotive will eventually be transferred to a new home for permanent display. The Purbeck Mineral and Mining Museum is currently being developed adjacent to Norden railway station as the destination.

Matt Wozniak (born January 6, 1983) is a Canadian curler from Winnipeg, Manitoba. He currently plays second on Team Jason Gunnlaugson. Wozniak is the former second for the Mike McEwen team which curled out of the Assiniboine Memorial Curling Club in Winnipeg.

Career

2005–2010
In 2005, Wozniak joined the new Mike McEwen rink that included Justin Richter and Andrew Melnuk. For the 2006-07 season, Richter and Melnuk left the team and were replaced with Geordie Hargreaves and Adam Guenther. The team disbanded after just one season together. Wozniak and McEwen joined with brothers Denni and B. J. Neufeld in 2007. In their first season together, they were a semi-finalist at the 2008 Safeway Championship, Manitoba's provincial championship. Their first Grand Slam event as a team was at the end season, at the 2008 Players' Championships. The team won two games, before being eliminated. At the conclusion of the 2008-09 season the McEwen team was ranked 7th on the CCA rankings. They had made it to three Grand Slam playoffs, and finished 4th at the 2009 Safeway Championship. During the 'Road to the Roar' 2009 Olympic Qualifier, the McEwen team just lost out to fellow Manitobans the Jason Gunnlaugson team in the semi-finals. Team McEwen thus missed out on the 2009 Canadian Olympic Curling Trials final despite being the favourite in that particular matchup vs Gunnlaugson. McEwen's rink made it to his first provincial final in 2010, when he lost to Jeff Stoughton in the 2010 Manitoba provincial final. The game was being played in Steinbach, Manitoba and as the Neufeld brothers and their father have roots in Steinbach, were treated very much as the home team and crowd favourites.

2010-2015: Grand Slam success and perennial provincial runner-up
Team McEwen started the 2010-11 season off well by defeating provincial rival Jeff Stoughton to win the World Cup of Curling and his first ever Grand Slam title in November, 2010. The achievement represented a breakthrough moment for the young squad that had been building momentum throughout the previous seasons. In part of the teams runner-up result in the provincial finals of 2010 and in part because of his 4 victories and leading the overall money winnings in the World Curling Tour season as of November 2010, the McEwen team was named as a nominee for the provincial team of the year by the Manitoba Sportswriters and Sportscasters Association. The team continued their strong season that year by defeating provincial rival Stoughton in the semi-final of the 2011 Canadian Open. They would then go on to beat the Glenn Howard team in the extra end of the final, thus winning their second career Grand Slam and their second of that season. Wozniak's rink once again made it to the Manitoba provincial this time, being the top seed (also ranked 1st in Canada). However, once again lost to Stoughton in the final of the 2011 Safeway Championship, losing by one point in the final end. The McEwen team then lost their third straight provincial final game at the 2012 Safeway Championship, this time losing to Rob Fowler, thus tying a provincial record for consecutive final losses previous set by Kerry Burtnyk from 97-99. This dubious record was avoided in 2013, when the McEwen rink failed to reach the final, but again losing to the rival Stoughton rink in the 2013 Safeway Championship semi-final. Once again, at the 2014 Safeway Championship, the team lost the final to Stoughton. The repeated disappointments at the provincial level created a narrative of unfulfilled potential despite the team's international success. Despite being ranked first in the world on both the World Curling Tour Order of Merit rankings and on the WCT money list, Wozniak lost his fifth provincial final in six years in 2015, losing to Reid Carruthers. The contrast between their dominance on the world stage and struggles at home became a defining characteristic of the team's legacy during this period.

Three Briers and team breakup 
Wozniak's rink won their first provincial title in 2016, sending them to their first Brier. The Matt Dunstone rink had committed themselves to the 2016 World Junior Curling Championships, which occurred at the same time as the 2016 Tim Hortons Brier, so when the Dunstone rink beat Reid Carruthers in the semi-final, McEwen's team would go to the Brier, even if they had lost to Dunstone. In 2017, Wozniak defended his Manitoba Championship by beating Reid Carruthers in the final. He would then better his 2016 Brier showing, going 9–2 in the round robin to enter the playoffs in first place and with hammer and choice of rocks (Brad Gushue was also 9–2 but lost first place due to losing his round robin meeting with Manitoba). He then lost 7–5 to Brad Gushue in the 1 vs. 2 game. In the semi finals against reigning Brier and World Champion Kevin Koe, they were in control for most of the game, being up 5–3 with hammer in the eighth end, but Koe made a comeback with a steal in the eighth end, two points in the tenth end, and another steal in the extra end, dropping Manitoba to the bronze medal game. They recovered to win their first Brier medal, defeating Brad Jacobs in their rematch of the 2016 bronze medal game, 7–6 in an extra end. While competing at the 2018 Viterra Championship, skip McEwen came down with chickenpox and was unable to play after the first game. B. J. Neufeld skipped the team, until a surprise appearance by McEwen in the final, where they lost to Carruthers. Despite the setback, they still had a chance to qualify for the 2018 Tim Hortons Brier through the wildcard game, which they won over Jason Gunnlaugson. Team McEwen had a difficult Brier and alongside Carruthers was unable to qualify for the playoffs. Following the Brier, the McEwen team announced they would be breaking up at the end of the 2017–18 season. Just days after the announcement, the McEwen team won the 2018 Elite 10 Grand Slam of Curling event, winning the top $28,000 prize money, and was the first team to go through the entire event undefeated. The Grand Slam victory was the team's seventh overall. The triumphant conclusion provided a bittersweet ending to one of Manitoba's most successful curling partnerships.

Wozniak took a few years off from men's play after Team McEwen broke up. However, he played mixed doubles with his current girlfriend Marlene Albrecht and spared for McEwen's new team. After Alex Forrest stepped away from competitive curling after the 2019–20 season, Wozniak joined the Jason Gunnlaugson rink. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic in Manitoba, the 2021 provincial championship was cancelled. As Team Gunnlaugson were the reigning provincial champions, they were chosen to represent Manitoba at the 2021 Tim Hortons Brier. At the Brier, they finished with a 6–6 record. The pandemic created unprecedented circumstances that altered traditional qualification pathways for major championships across Canada.

Personal life
Wozniak is employed as a mortgage broker for Vertuity Mortgage. He is currently in a relationship with Swiss curler Marlene Albrecht and has two children. His professional work outside curling has provided financial stability throughout his competitive career.
