Solar power is a wonderful thing from modern science. There is one tiny little problem, however. It's still more expensive than using other kinds of power. If it wasn't for the cost, it would be a much better idea, but then that goes for all kinds of power that can be made again and again.

Many people will point out that putting in solar power is on par with or even cheaper than building new power plants, like nuclear or coal. While this is true in the very large scale, you're probably not going to build your own power plant, and therefore don't have that expense to deal with.

Look at the cost of a solar panel compared to how much power *on average* it can make. Do the math and see for yourself what the numbers say.

> I believe if the government put in some money they could easily shut down one or two nuclear power plants

You seem to be working under some false ideas. First, the government is helping to pay for solar power purchases in California in a huge way - so they *are* putting in some money. Second, the government does not run the Nuclear Power Plants - those are run by private companies. They are *watched over* by the government. Also, the main cost of a nuclear power plant is the building of the plant and the getting rid of the nuclear material - not the running of the plant itself. Shutting down a working plant would waste money, not save money.

Like I said, I love solar power, for all kinds of reasons. It's "point of use" which means there is very little loss due to long distance movement of power. It's almost zero bad gases going into the air. It's silent and makes no noise (that's a big thing for me). It gives the greatest benefit when the need is the highest, in the summer, in the daytime.

Possibly the best use of solar might be to run air cooling systems. During the summer when the sun is strong, the need for air is strong. Use the light gathered by solar panels to help cool the building. Also, if the panels are on the roof, they give shade for the building. Win/win.

Still, on a pure cost compared to benefit look at the facts, however, it's still cheaper to use coal or natural gas to make electricity.

Say you're a seller living in 17th century Amsterdam, and there's a bunch of super-rich ladies who really, really loves cumin (as in, the spice). Unfortunately, cumin doesn't grow anywhere near Amsterdam, you have to go to the middle east or India to get some of that fine stuff so it's *super-expensive*. Over there, however, it grows like a weed and costs very little money. If only you could get some of that cheap cumin over to Amsterdam, you could make a lot of money!

Unfortunately, the only way to do that is to send out a big-ass ship for like nine months. Not only is that HUGELY expensive (you have to get a ship, and a captain and crew who all wants nine months worth of pay), but it is also really risky. The boat could sink, after all, or all the cumin could spoil and go bad.

So how do you do this? Assuming you're not amazingly rich yourself (and very few people or groups, aside from maybe whole nations, are that rich), how do you pay for this? You could go to a bank or money-lender and take out a loan, a loan which would have a very steep interest rate that could almost eat up all of your profits. And what if the boat sank? You'd be completely broke, and be thrown into prison, if the money-lender doesn't waste your broke ass first.

So, you come up with an idea. You can't pay for this trip alone. But you could rather easily pay for, say, one tenth of the cost of the trip. And look at that, you have nine friends, all of whom could also afford one tenth of the cost of the trip. So you all come to an agreement: you decide to each pay for part of the cost for the trip (i.e. you "buy stock" in the business), each getting shares worth one tenth of the total business. With this money, you pay for the boat and crew, send them off, and then nine months later, it comes back with a cargo-hold full of delicious, super-expensive cumin. The profits far and away make up for the starting cost, and each of you and your friends gets one tenth of the huge profits.

But what happens if your boat sinks? Well, it's a real bummer obviously (especially for the crew!), but you only paid for one tenth of the cost, and this was a cost you could afford to eat, you're not gonna get killed over it. Since the risk was spread around to 10 people, no one landed in debtors prison. Everyone took a small hit, instead of one person taking an huge hit.

Think about this example, and all the people involved in it. The fancy ladies got their cumin (and for cheaper than they would have otherwise). The shipwrights got work building a new ship. The captain and crew all got work and a salary. The trader in India got a new customer for his cumin. And obviously, you and your friends got really rich in the process. In short, *every single person is better off*, and it wouldn't have happened if this idea of "buying and selling stocks" didn't exist.

This is the advantage of a stock market. It moves money around from where it just lies around doing absolutely nothing to where it can be put to use, and in the meantime, everybody gets richer. It also spreads risk between lots of people, so you don't have to be afraid of going broke all the time.

Now, obviously, there are problems with how the modern day American version of the stock market works. But the complaint is that it stopped doing what doing what it is supposed to be doing (i.e. moving money around so that it can be put into useful work) and stopped being a means to an end, and it became an end unto itself. The basic idea of a stock market is a great idea, and you'd have to be a real hard-core communist to be against it. It is why we have railroads, cars, computers, telephones, cheap and plenty of food, medicine, and all the other modern things we value so highly.

Depends on if your business is a sole ownership, single member LLC, multi member LLC, an LLC with the "S" tax choice, an S Corporation, or a C Corporation.

Sole Ownership: All profits and losses pass to you as an individual. You're also personally responsible for anything that goes wrong. Helpful Tip: form an LLC or go get a free meeting with a business lawyer.

Single Member LLC: Profits and losses pass through to you personally, but your responsibility is limited to the Company's property. You also have to pay self employment tax.

Multi-Member LLC: Profits and losses are split in relation to each members ownership interest in the company. You also pay self employment tax.

LLC with "S" choice: You pay yourself a reasonable salary, and that salary is not subject to the self employment tax. Remaining profits and losses are passed through to you and any other shareholders in relation to each shareholders percentage interest in the corporation. Whether or not you get taxed on any payments depends on your basis, but this is where it gets complicated and I can't explain it like you're five years old. Just let the accountant worry about this part.

S Corporation: see above

C Corporation: The corporations profits are taxed at the corporate tax level and then any payments made to shareholders are taxed as well. This is called double taxation and it's why C Corporations are not perfect for small business owners.

Not Ethical Life Helpful Tip: Want to live a fancy lifestyle, completely tax free, and without much hard work? Start a non-profit seed faith mega church, go on TV, and convince all the followers to send your church money, because god will take the little seed of faith they send and will grow the seed into ten times the amount they sent.

The energy of the clap remains unchanged so we look at where that energy is going. In a regular clap on earth, the energy of the hitting goes into a variety of things; 

1) sound 

 2) bending of your hands

3) heat

4) some others that are probably constant in both situations and I won't talk about

Let's make a picture (very roughly) of a clap. 2 hands, each at 500g moving at 2m/s. E=mv2 so E= 4J roughly. 

Even though a clap would be thought of as a bouncing hitting there is likely some small energy loss to bending. I would expect to see some damage to tiny living pieces under a tool that makes things look bigger but very little. The biggest user of energy is going to be the heat given off. From [here](_URL_0_) we see a clap is about 20ms long (very rough) and from [here](_URL_1_) we can see the sound power of a few similar things, let's say an alarm clock is close enough. Even if we're wrong by a number of a 100x, it's still close enough for this talk. By doing the roughest, dirtiest adding up of the sound wave shown in the first link with the power output of the table in the second, we get a total energy of 2x10^-6 J of energy from a clap. Compared the the 4J of input energy into the hitting, on earth, the sound energy is only 0.00005% of the total let out. The rest goes to heat and bending, and I wouldn't even bother guessing at what the amount is between those. 


So, to answer your question: 

On earth, only 0.00005% of the energy goes into the sound of a clap. The rest goes into heat and bending of your hands. In space, 0% of the energy goes into sound and that tiny bit that would have gone into sound on earth simply goes into more heat. The energy of the sound of the clap is so low by comparison to the heat given off by the hitting to start with that the action is basically unchanged except you hear no sound.

Depends on your guesses, but the worst case is certainly bad. Here are some guesses of worldwide average climate change. Most of this change will happen near the poles and in the oceans.

What does this sort of warming look like? As an example, the warmest period in earth's history in the last few hundred million years was the Cretaceous. During this time, around 100-65 million years ago, CO2 amounts were around 1000 parts per million, and worldwide temperature was around 10 degrees Celsius higher than today. Releases and temperature changes that begin to get close to these levels are certainly not out of the question by the end of next century, though the chance of that sort of situation is open to argument.

During the Cretaceous, sea levels were hundreds of meters higher than they are right now. Central North America was underwater beneath a shallow inland sea. And trees that lose their leaves grew in regions at the poles. The high temperatures also greatly increased the strength and number of harmful weather events like hurricanes and typhoons. Under these sorts of situations, most of the hot regions near the equator would be impossible to live in or very unpleasant because of heat and wetness in the air, large parts of land would be completely underwater pushing out hundreds of millions or billions of people, fresh water would become hard to find as all ice river sources melted completely, and the northern regions of the Canadian wilderness would have climates like the Mediterranean. This does not go into the huge changes in ocean saltiness and acid levels which would cause the widespread dying off of ocean wildlife (which is a major food source for humans), and the widespread dying off of a huge number of kinds of living things unable to change or move quickly enough to new regions. Animals that travel seasonally would be similarly troubled, and huge human movements to currently mild zones (that would become hot or somewhat hot) would destroy the environments supporting many millions of other kinds of living things.
words_common_s.coling::8e0f7cff-07ca-48c6-b381-34b577d1: Before babies start to use language they form speech through babble. Basically they play with making noise through open and closed mouths. These are the easiest sounds for growing babies to make as they explore sounds. Think of the open and closed mouths like binary code: 0 equals the open vowel sound, like 'aaaaaa'. Then 1, or in our case a closed mouth, equals the closed consonant sound, like 'm' or 'p'. Try it. Close your mouth as if you were making the beginning of an 'm' or 'p' word, then just open your mouth and push through some air. You're basically making the 'ma' and 'pa' sounds. 'B', 'D', and 'P' are pretty much the same as closed consonants. That's why we see the differences found: baba, abba, papa, dada, and so on. So, these are the basic building blocks of making sounds with the voice, so they are the ones babies use. The simplest form for the human mouth to make. Another interesting question is that these babies who don't yet use language have been the ones to give birth to language in the naming of mother and father. Why did we follow their lead? Maybe the simple naming of 'poo' and 'wee' in many languages follow a similar reason. I think grandparents also have similar binary forms in many languages too, like in Hindi. Paternal Grandfather — दादा (daadaa) Paternal Grandmother — दादी (daadii) Maternal Grandfather — नाना (naanaa) Maternal Grandmother — नानी (naanii). These patterns show up again and again across different languages around the world, which tells us something important about how humans naturally learn to speak and communicate with each other from the very earliest age.
words_common_s.coling::97ce3bac-5618-4fcb-8600-bcf08ed8: To be blunt, unless you're very experienced with wines, you probably won't be able to look at 2 similar wine bottles and right away figure out which one you'll like better. What you can do is figure out what kind of wines you like in general. To figure out which wine types you like, you have to actually try a few of those wines. Unfortunately, this can cost some money. Also, if you're actually 5, then it's against the law to buy wine in the US. Wines are generally divided by where the grapes were grown and the type of grape (called the wine's "varietal"). Common Red Types: Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinot Noir, Merlot, Syrah (sometimes called Shiraz), Zinfandel Common White Types: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Gris (sometimes called Pinot Grigio), Riesling, Gewurztraminer When you taste wines, pay attention to what you like about them. For example, many red wines have a clear taste that makes your mouth feel dry. This is known as a "tannic" taste (because it's caused by tiny things called tannins). If you like tannic wines, a tannic type, like Cabernet Sauvignon, might be good for you. For white wines, common easy to notice features include sharpness (sourness) and sugar content. You probably don't need an explanation of what counts as sour or sugary. Another common feature to look for in red or white wine is "oakiness". If you smell a wood-like smell in the wine, that means that the wine has an "oaky" flavor. With all this in mind, remember that there's no such thing as a wine that everyone thinks is great. All that matters is which kind you like best, even if that means choosing to drink a $10 jug of wine over a $500 bottle of fancy Cabernet from Bordeaux. Also, when in doubt, ask the waiter, wine expert, or wine shop worker to help you out. Usually if you have a rough idea of what you want, they can help you find something you'd like in your price range. The key is to be open to trying different wines and learning what tastes good to you personally without worrying about what other people think is the best choice.

words_common_s.coling::f249dac3-f3a2-4db9-9758-e18c9f8f: There are a bunch of people in a town. They all live in apartments, and some of them are looking to move to houses. The house builders in this town see this desire and start building houses. When they look for people to buy these houses, there is a lot of desire, so this can push prices higher as there is more competition for supply. (the opposite of competition on the supply side, where it brings prices down) A bunch of people buy houses at these high desire prices, and prices continue to climb as desire remains high. But, once the price gets too high, or most of the desire goes away from everyone wanting a house having one, there suddenly becomes much lower desire, dropping the cost of buying a house. Those that have already bought a house now are seeing themselves as losing money, and want to move back into an apartment while getting rid of the house; this turns up supply, causing a very fast drop in prices for these houses. It continues until the prices reach a level that desire begins to become steady at a new level. When we talk about a bubble, it really comes down to a market of low supply and high desire quickly changing to a high supply and low desire market. The major problem is that both versions help themselves keep going in that direction: high desire brings people in to invest and take advantage of the price increases, while low desire gets people to try to push away from the market, making supply even higher. This makes the whole thing worse because when prices are going up, more people want to join in and buy, and when prices are going down, more people want to leave and sell. The back and forth movement keeps getting bigger until something stops it.
words_common_s.coling::f4f3b137-0da5-4cc5-a8e0-08f5a284: You can't think of the signals as digital in a wire when you send at high speed. You have to think of the signal as an ongoing changing signal. Signals don't change right away from 1 to 0 and they need time to travel in a cable. A signal in a cat 5 cable travels at 0.64 times the speed of light or 4.8 to 5.3 ns per meter. For 100Mbit ethernet, that means 100 times 10 to the power of 6 bits per second, which equals 100 bits in 1000 ns, which equals 1 bit in 10 ns. So if the ethernet cable is longer than 2 meters there are more than one bit in the cable at the same time. A cable can be 100 meters long so there will be 50 bits in the cable at once. So the signal is clearly not the same in the whole cable at the same time. The bitrate in the cable is in real life higher because of the way data is packaged. This is a picture of how a 100Mbit ethernet signal looks like in reality. URL_1 Here you have an eye picture where you put different signals on top of each other. URL_0 The way to look at it is that the system has to figure out if the signal is at the top, in the middle, or at the bottom where the black empty spaces are. You can see that it is messy and the holes, which we call eyes, are quite small. The smaller the eyes are, the harder it is to figure out where the signal is, and if they go away you can't pick up the signal anymore. So now when you see that the signal is messy and always changing, you are starting to understand that you need cables that act in certain ways. How a signal moves forward depends on the distance between the wires and the width of the wires and other material along the wire and by other things too. There will be noise from the area around and the other wire pairs, so the wire has to be twisted at different rates compared to each other to reduce the noise. So to have a wire with known qualities that works with the equipment, you have to have a shared set of rules. You can run the signal over other wires if you know what you are doing. Look at this show with barbed wire URL_2. There is a reason that the barbed wire pairs are close to each other and running side by side and the pairs are far apart from other pairs. I have read a written piece about this that I can't find that explained that barbed wire in that arrangement has a similar effect on the signal as a cat 5 cable does. If the wires in the pairs would have not been running side by side or the pairs been closer together, it would have not worked at all.

words_common_s.coling::817b2dbf-699e-4bec-825a-2bbdf598: An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is a key computer security tool for network managers as it finds harmful traffic and computer attacks. With the recent wins of machine learning methods such as deep learning, more and more IDS are now using machine learning programs to find attacks faster. However, these systems lack strength when facing types of attacks they have never seen before. With the growing number of new attacks, especially against Internet of Things devices, having a strong IDS able to spot unusual and new attacks becomes needed. This work looks at the chance of using opposing model systems to make machine learning based IDS stronger and more reliable. More specifically, we offer a new method named SIGMA, that uses opposing examples to make IDS stronger against new types of attacks. Using Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) and problem-solving search methods, SIGMA creates opposing examples, one step at a time, and uses it to retrain a machine learning-based IDS, until the finding rate stops getting better, meaning until the detection system is not improving anymore and has reached its best level. A round of improvement consists of a creating phase, in which we use GANs and problem-solving search methods to create new instances; a judging phase in which we measure the finding rate of those newly created attacks; and a training phase, in which we train the IDS with those attacks. We have tested the SIGMA method for four standard machine learning sorting programs acting as IDS, with a mixture of GAN and a mixed local-search and genetic program, to create new collections of attacks. Our results show that SIGMA can successfully create opposing attacks against different machine learning based IDS. Also, using SIGMA, we can make the performance of an IDS better up to one hundred percent after as little as two rounds of improvement.
words_common_s.coling::0a6f4d1d-1792-4bfc-a4cf-9fcf0636: Tree family maps are leaf-named one-way graphs without loops that are used to describe family histories that don't look like trees and are thus a wider version of tree family maps. The mixing number of a tree family map is the total of all incoming paths minus the number of points plus one. The Mixing Number problem takes as input a group of tree family maps and asks to build a tree family map that contains a copy of each of the input trees and has the smallest possible mixing number. We present a step-by-step method for the Mixing Number problem on three two-part tree family maps on n leaves, which runs in time O of c to the k power times poly of n, with k the mixing number of a best possible map and c some positive whole number. For the case of two trees, a step-by-step method with running time O of 3.18 to the k power times n was offered before whereas a step-by-step method with running time O of c to the k power times poly of n for more than two trees had before this article stayed out of reach. The step-by-step method for two trees uses the close link to loop-free agreement woods to reach a straight line power in the running time, while earlier step-by-step methods for more than two trees clearly or not clearly relied on a rough force search through all possible basic map shapes, leading to running times that are not O of c to the k power times poly of n, for any c. The link to loop-free agreement woods is much weaker for more than two trees, so even given the right agreement wood, the rebuilding of the map creates major problems. We show new basic results that allow us to rebuild a map without having to guess the basic shape. Our methods work for more than three input trees except for one key statement that matches points in the map to tree points and, in this way, makes smallest the amount of guessing involved in building the map. The main open problem is therefore to show results that create such a matching for more than three trees.
words_common_s.coling::0c653e8b-8157-47f3-bdaa-142023fb: We introduce the binary value rule which is a simple addition problem example expressing that a natural number written in binary cannot be negative, relating it to main problems in proof and math complexity. We prove conditional higher than any polynomial lower bounds on the Ideal Proof System (IPS) refutation size of this example, based on a well-known guess by Shub and Smale about the hardness of computing factorials, where IPS is the strong math proof system introduced by Grochow and Pitassi. On the other hand, we show that short IPS refutations of this example bridge the gap between strong enough math and half-math proof systems. Our results extend to complete IPS the approach introduced in Forbes et al., whereby lower bounds against parts of IPS were obtained using restricted math circuit lower bounds, and show that the binary value rule captures the advantage of half-math over math reasoning, for strong enough systems. In particular, we show the following: Conditional IPS lower bounds: item Conditional IPS lower bounds: The Shub-Smale guess implies a higher than any polynomial lower bound on the size of IPS refutations of the binary value rule over the rationals defined as the cannot be satisfied straight equation i 1 n 2 - i 1 x i - 1, for boolean x i 's. Further, the related -guess implies a higher than any polynomial lower bound on the size of IPS refutations of a variant of the binary value rule over the ring of rational functions. No prior conditional lower bounds were known for IPS or for apparently much weaker statement proof systems such as Frege. 1 1 footnote 1 Though simple, the binary value rule is not a direct translation of a boolean formula, hence, similar to and other results on math proofs (e.g., Razborov), IPS lower bounds on this rule do not necessarily lead to lower bounds for Frege or its parts. Math vs. half-math proofs: item Math vs. half-math proofs: Admitting short refutations of the binary value rule is necessary for any math proof system to fully copy any known half-math proof system, and for strong enough math proof systems it is also enough. In particular, we introduce a very strong proof system that copies all known half-math proof systems (and most other known concrete statement proof systems), under the name Cone Proof System (CPS), as a half-math similar version of the ideal proof system: CPS establishes the cannot be satisfied nature of collections of polynomial equalities and inequalities over the reals, by representing sum-of-squares proofs (and extensions) as math circuits. We prove that IPS is in polynomial time the same as CPS if and only if IPS admits polynomial-size refutations of the binary value rule (for the language of systems of equations that have no 01-solutions), over both Z and Q.
words_common_s.coling::a098aa01-9d81-40a6-8321-ca3d4a88: Graph-Laplacians and their visual number-based mappings play an important role in many areas of machine learning. This paper is focused on graph-Laplacian size reduction for the visual number-based grouping of data as a main use, however, it can also be used in data mining, data shape learning, and other tasks. Visual number-based mapping provides a low-size measurement of the data shape which makes the following task (for example, grouping with k-means or any of its similar versions) much easier. However, despite reducing the number of measurements of data, the total computing cost may still be too expensive for large data sets because of two reasons. First, computing the partial breaking down into basic parts of the graph-Laplacian usually requires a large mathematical working space. Second, after the visual number-based mapping is complete, one still has to work with the same number of data points, which may destroy the usefulness of the method. For example, grouping of the mapped data is usually done with different relaxed versions of k-means which computing cost grows badly with respect to the size of data set. Also, they become likely to get stuck in local best solutions that are not the overall best, so their strength depends on the choice of starting guess. In this work, we switch the focus from the whole data set to a smaller part of graph points, which we call the target smaller part. We create two new step-by-step methods for such low-size representation of the original graph that keeps important overall distances between the points of the target smaller part. In particular, it allows us to make sure that target smaller part grouping matches with the visual number-based grouping of the full data set if one would do such grouping. That is reached by a properly measured smaller working model of the graph-Laplacian that copies closely the spreading transfer function of the original graph for inputs and outputs limited to the target smaller part. Working with a small target smaller part reduces greatly the required size of mathematical working space and allows us to use the usual step-by-step methods (like similar versions of k-means) in the situations when they are most strong and useful. This was checked in the number-based grouping tests with both made-up and real data. We also note that our smaller working model method can be used in a purely transfer-function-data-driven way, so it becomes the only possible choice for extremely large graphs that are not directly reachable. There are several uses for our step-by-step methods. First, they can be used on their own for representative smaller part grouping in cases when handling the full graph is either not possible or simply not needed. Second, they may be used for quality checking. Third, as they hugely reduce the problem size, they make possible the use of more complex step-by-step methods for the task being looked at (like more powerful similar versions of k-means based on half-clear mathematical planning instead of the usual Lloyd's step-by-step method). Finally, they can be used as building blocks of a many-level divide-and-beat type step-by-step method to handle the full graph. The last use will be reported in a separate article.
words_common_s.coling::d9b96a87-ee9b-46e9-995f-edfccd85: We look at the problem of designing [ n , k ] straight-line codes for shared storage systems (DSS) that satisfy the (r , t) - Local Repair Property , where any t ( t) at the same time failed nodes can be locally repaired, each with locality r . The numbers n , k , r , t are positive whole numbers such that r k n and t - n k . We look at the working repair model and the one-after-another approach for repairing many failed nodes. By working repair, we mean that the packet stored in each newcomer is not always an exact copy of the lost data but a symbol that keeps the (r , t) -local repair property. By the one-after-another approach, we mean that the t newcomers are ordered in a proper sequence such that each newcomer can be repaired from the live nodes and the newcomers that are ordered before it. Such codes, which we call (n , k , r , t) -working locally repairable codes (FLRC), are the most general class of LRCs and contain several smaller classes of LRCs reported in the books and papers. In this paper, we aim to make the best the storage overhead (in other words, the code rate) of FLRCs. We find a lower limit on the code length n given t {2 , 3 } and any possible k , r . For t 2 , our limit makes more general the rate limit proved in . For t 3 , our limit makes better the rate limit proved in . We also give some ways to build exact LRCs for t {2 , 3 } whose length n reaches the limit of (n , k , r , t) -FLRC, which proves the tightness of our limits and also means that there is no gap between the best code length of working LRCs and exact LRCs for certain sets of numbers. What is more, our ways to build are over the binary field, so they are of interest in real use and practice today.
words_common_s.coling::60c879b9-6ebb-4551-8f22-52c6a144: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) is the problem of building a map of a moving agent's surroundings while finding the agent's position within the map. Dense SLAM methods perform building and finding position at pixel detail level. These methods require a lot of computer power, which has blocked their use on low-power devices with limited resources. Rough computing can be used to speed up SLAM work as long as the rough estimates do not stop the agent from moving correctly through the surroundings. Earlier studies of rough estimates in SLAM have thought that the entire path of the agent is known before the agent starts, and they have looked at offline controls that set rough estimate settings at the start of the path. In practice, the path is usually not known ahead of time, and allowing settings to change on the fly opens up more chances for cutting down computing time and energy. In this paper, we describe SLAMBooster, a system that is aware of the task, an online control system for dense SLAM that adjusts rough estimate settings during the movement of the agent. SLAMBooster is built on a control method called proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller but our tests showed this controller that ignores the task led to an unacceptable drop in position finding accuracy. To fix this problem, SLAMBooster also uses area knowledge for controlling rough estimates by doing smooth surface finding and position correction. We built SLAMBooster in the open-source SLAMBench tool and tested it on more than a dozen paths from both the published work and our own study. Our tests show that on the average, SLAMBooster cuts the computing time by 72 and energy use by 35 on an embedded platform, while keeping the accuracy of finding position within reasonable limits. These improvements make it possible to use SLAM on a wider range of devices.
words_common_s.coling::6b54ef51-f42e-4ac2-840e-6b536faa: While the Commission has a sole right to start new laws, the European Parliament and the Council of the European Union have powers to change and block laws during the lawmaking process. According to the Treaty on European Union articles 9 and 10, the EU follows "the principle of equality of its citizens" and is meant to be founded on "representative democracy." In practice, equality and democracy are lacking because the elected representatives in the Parliament cannot start laws against the Commission's wishes, citizens of smallest countries have ten times the voting weight in Parliament as citizens of the largest countries, and "qualified majorities" or agreement of the Council are required to make laws. The reason for this "democratic deficit" under the Treaties is usually thought to be that complete joining together of the European economy and political institutions required the technical coordination of experts, while popular understanding of the EU developed and nationalist feelings declined after the war. Over time, this has meant the Parliament gradually gained more say: from being an unelected assembly, to its first direct elections in 1979, to having increasingly more rights in the lawmaking process. Citizens' rights are therefore limited compared to the democratic political systems within all European member states: under TEU article 11 citizens and groups have the rights such as making their views public and submit a proposal that must be considered by the Commission with one million signatures. TFEU article 227 contains a further right for citizens to ask the Parliament on issues which affect them. Parliament elections take place every five years, and votes for Members of the European Parliament in member states must be organized by proportional representation or a single transferable vote. There are 750 MEPs and their numbers are "degressively proportional" according to member state size. This means - although the Council is meant to be the body representing member states - in the Parliament citizens of smaller member states have more voice than citizens in larger member states. MEPs divide, as they do in national Parliaments, along political party lines: the conservative European People's Party is currently the largest, and the Party of European Socialists leads the opposition. Parties do not receive public money from the EU, as the Court of Justice held in Parti ecologiste "Les Verts" v Parliament that this was entirely an issue to be controlled by the member states. The Parliament's powers include calling investigations into bad management or appoint an Ombudsman waiting for any court proceedings. It can require the Commission respond to questions and by a two-thirds majority can criticize the whole Commission (as happened to the Santer Commission in 1999). In some cases, the Parliament has clear consultation rights, which the Commission must genuinely follow. However its role taking part in the lawmaking process still remains limited because no member can actually start or pass laws without the Commission and Council, meaning power is not in the hands of directly elected representatives of the people: in the EU it is not yet true that "the administration is in the hands of the many and not of the few."
words_common_s.coling::049da962-b4ab-4271-80d7-6c08dd71: Despite Martin Luther's harsh attacks against his Roman Catholic opponents over issues concerning Mary and the saints, religious scholars appear to agree that Luther followed the Marian decisions of the church-wide meetings and beliefs of the church. He held fast to the belief that Mary was a lifelong virgin and the Theotokos or Mother of God. Special attention is given to the claim that Luther, some three-hundred years before the official acceptance of the Immaculate Conception by Pope Pius IX in 1854, was a firm believer of that view. Others say that Luther in later years changed his position on the Immaculate Conception, which, at that time was not clearly defined in the Church, keeping however the sinlessness of Mary throughout her life. For Luther, early in his life, the Assumption of Mary was an understood fact, although he later stated that the Bible did not say anything about it and stopped celebrating its feast day. Important to him was the belief that Mary and the saints do live on after death. "Throughout his career as a priest-professor-reformer, Luther preached, taught, and argued about the worship of Mary with a wordiness that ranged from childlike faith to complicated attacks. His views are closely linked to his Christocentric teaching and its results for church services and faith." He considered the Roman Catholic practice of celebrating saints' days and making requests for help addressed especially to Mary and other departed saints to be idol worship. A digital signature is a mathematical way for checking the realness of digital messages or documents. A valid digital signature, where the requirements are met, gives a receiver very high confidence that the message was created by a known sender (realness), and that the message was not changed in transit (wholeness).

Digital signatures are a standard part of most secret-code method groups, and are commonly used for software sharing, financial deals, contract management software, and in other cases where it is important to find fakery or meddling with content.

Digital signatures are often used to put into practice electronic signatures, which includes any electronic data that carries the purpose of a signature, but not all electronic signatures use digital signatures. Electronic signatures have legal meaning in some countries, including Canada, South Africa, the United States, Algeria, Turkey, India, Brazil, Indonesia, Mexico, Saudi Arabia, Uruguay, Switzerland, Chile and the countries of the European Union.

Digital signatures use two-sided secret writing. In many cases, they provide a layer of checking and safety to messages sent through a non-safe channel: Properly put into practice, a digital signature gives the receiver reason to believe the message was sent by the claimed sender. Digital signatures are the same as traditional handwritten signatures in many ways, but properly put into practice digital signatures are more hard to fake than the handwritten type. Digital signature methods, in the sense used here, are based on secret writing, and must be put into practice properly to be effective. They can also provide non-denial, meaning that the signer cannot successfully claim they did not sign a message, while also claiming their private key remains secret. Further, some non-denial plans offer a time stamp for the digital signature, so that even if the private key is shown to others, the signature is valid. Digitally signed messages may be anything shown as a bitstring: examples include electronic mail, contracts, or a message sent through some other secret-writing method.

Speech recognition is a mixed-subject area of computer science and computer language study that creates methods and tools that make it possible for computers to recognize and change spoken language into text with the main benefit of being able to search through it. It is also known as automatic speech recognition (ASR), computer speech recognition or speech to text (STT). It brings together knowledge and study in the computer science, language study and computer engineering areas. The opposite process is speech creation.

Some speech recognition systems need "training" (also called "enrollment") where a single speaker reads text or separate words into the system. The system studies the person's particular voice and uses it to improve the recognition of that person's speech, leading to better correctness. Systems that do not use training are called "speaker-independent" systems. Systems that use training are called "speaker dependent".

Speech recognition uses include voice user screens such as voice dialing (for example "call home"), call routing (for example "I would like to make a collect call"), home device control, search key words (for example find a podcast where certain words were spoken), simple data entry (for example, entering a credit card number), making of organized documents (for example a radiology report), finding out speaker features, speech-to-text handling (for example, word processors or emails), and aircraft (usually called direct voice input).

The term voice recognition or speaker identification means identifying the speaker, rather than what they are saying. Recognizing the speaker can make easier the task of changing speech in systems that have been trained on a particular person's voice or it can be used to check or confirm the identity of a speaker as part of a security process.

From the technology viewpoint, speech recognition has a long history with several waves of major new ideas. Most recently, the field has gained from progress in deep learning and big data. The progress is shown not only by the rise of school papers published in the field, but more importantly by the worldwide business adoption of a range of deep learning methods in designing and putting into use speech recognition systems.

Control theory is a field of mathematics that deals with the control of changing systems in built processes and machines. The goal is to develop a model or set of rules governing the use of system inputs to drive the system to a wanted state, while making smaller any delay, overshoot, or steady-state error and making sure a level of control stability; often with the aim to reach a degree of best performance.
To do this, a controller with the needed corrective behavior is required. This controller watches the controlled process variable (PV), and compares it with the reference or set point (SP). The difference between actual and wanted value of the process variable, called the error signal, or SP-PV error, is used as feedback to create a control action to bring the controlled process variable to the same value as the set point. Other aspects which are also studied are controllability and observability. Control theory is used in control system engineering to design automation that have changed manufacturing, aircraft, communications and other industries, and created new fields such as robotics.
Wide use is usually made of a picture style known as the block diagram. In it the transfer function, also known as the system function or network function, is a mathematical model of the relation between the input and output based on the equations describing the system that show rates of change over time.
Control theory dates from the 19th century, when the basis in theory for the operation of governors was first described by James Clerk Maxwell. Control theory was further moved forward by Edward Routh in 1874, Charles Sturm and in 1895, Adolf Hurwitz, who all gave their part to the setting up of control stability measures; and from 1922 onwards, the development of PID control theory by Nicolas Minorsky.
Although a major use of mathematical control theory is in control systems engineering, which deals with the design of process control systems for industry, other uses range far beyond this. As the general theory of feedback systems, control theory is helpful wherever feedback occurs - thus control theory also has uses in life sciences, computer engineering, sociology and operations research.
words_common_s.coling::5293d27b-2991-4ca1-93ab-e336d0eb:
Drug design, often called rational drug design or simply rational design, is the creative process of finding new medicines based on the knowledge of a biological target. The drug is most commonly a natural small molecule that turns on or turns off the function of a biological molecule such as a protein, which in turn results in a healing benefit to the patient. In the most basic sense, drug design involves the design of molecules that are matching in shape and charge to the biological molecule target with which they interact and therefore will attach to it. Drug design frequently but not always depends on computer modeling methods. This type of modeling is sometimes called computer-aided drug design. Finally, drug design that depends on the knowledge of the three-dimensional structure of the biological molecule target is known as structure-based drug design. In addition to small molecules, biological medicines including peptides and especially healing antibodies are an increasingly important group of drugs and computer methods for improving the attraction, pickiness, and steadiness of these protein-based healing treatments have also been developed.

The phrase "drug design" is to some degree a wrong name. A more accurate term is ligand design (that is, design of a molecule that will attach tightly to its target). Although design methods for guessing binding attraction are reasonably successful, there are many other properties, such as biological availability, metabolic half-life, side effects, and so on, that first must be improved before a ligand can become a safe and effective drug. These other features are often difficult to guess with rational design methods. Nevertheless, because of high failure rates, especially during clinical phases of drug development, more attention is being focused early in the drug design process on selecting candidate drugs whose physical and chemical properties are guessed to result in fewer problems during development and hence more likely to lead to an approved, marketed drug. Furthermore, laboratory experiments combined with computer methods are increasingly used in early drug discovery to select compounds with more favorable ADME (absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion) and poisonous profiles.
words_common_s.coling::d2400f57-c1e4-49a6-aaa9-1c92f181:
Data dredging (also known as data snooping or p-hacking)[a] is the misuse of data analysis to find patterns in data that can be presented as having real importance, thus greatly increasing and understating the risk of false positives. This is done by performing many tests on the data and only reporting those that come back with important results.

The process of data dredging involves testing many different ideas using a single data set by completely searching—perhaps for combinations of things that might show a connection, and perhaps for groups of cases or observations that show differences in their average or in their breakdown by some other thing.

Common tests of real importance are based on the chance that a particular result would happen if luck alone were at work, and must accept some risk of wrong conclusions of a certain type (wrong rejections of the null idea). This level of risk is called the importance level. When large numbers of tests are performed, some produce false results of this type; hence 5% of randomly chosen ideas might be (wrongly) reported to be really important at the 5% importance level, 1% might be (wrongly) reported to be really important at the 1% importance level, and so on, by chance alone. When enough ideas are tested, it is almost certain that some will be reported to be really important (even though this is misleading), since almost every data set with any amount of randomness is likely to contain (for example) some false connections. If they are not careful, researchers using data mining methods can be easily misled by these results.

Data dredging is an example of ignoring the multiple comparisons problem. One form is when smaller groups are compared without telling the reader about the total number of smaller group comparisons examined.

Carnegie Mellon University (CMU) is a private research university in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. One of its earlier forms was started in 1900 by Andrew Carnegie as the Carnegie Technical Schools; it became the Carnegie Institute of Technology in 1912 and began giving four-year degrees in the same year. In 1967, the Carnegie Institute of Technology joined together with the Mellon Institute of Industrial Research, started in 1913 by Andrew Mellon and Richard B. Mellon and earlier a part of the University of Pittsburgh.[10] Carnegie Mellon University has worked as a single school since the joining together.

The university is made up of seven colleges and separate schools: The College of Engineering, College of Fine Arts, Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences, Mellon College of Science, Tepper School of Business, Heinz College of Information Systems and Public Policy, and the School of Computer Science.[11][12] The university has its main grounds located 5 miles (8 km) from Downtown Pittsburgh. It also has over a dozen degree-giving locations in six continents, including degree-giving grounds in Qatar, Silicon Valley, and Kigali, Rwanda (Carnegie Mellon University Africa) and working relationships with universities across the United States and in the United Kingdom, Portugal, Japan, China, Mexico, and Italy.[13]

Carnegie Mellon is known for its progress in research and new fields of study, especially being home to many firsts in computer science (including the first computer science, machine learning, and robotics departments), leading the way in the field of management science,[14] and being home to the first drama program in the United States. CMU is placed among "R1: Doctoral Universities – Very High Research Activity".[15] In 2020, the university had research and development spending of $386 million.[16] Past and present teachers and former students include 20 Nobel Prize winners, 13 Turing Award winners, 26 members of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, 39 fellows of the American Association for the Advancement of Science, 91 members of the National Academies, 142 Emmy Award winners, 52 Tony Award winners, and 12 Academy Award winners.[17] Carnegie Mellon takes in 15,818 students across its many grounds from 117 countries, pays more than 1,400 teachers, and has an active group of former students of over 112,000.[18]

Yes, you wish your mother was sweet, gentle, understanding, kind, but no matter what don't be disrespectful. Just don't say your feelings in front of her. It will only make things worse for you. There's a very good chance your mother knows she's not very smart, and that makes her act in mean ways. Reminding her of her problems will not make life easier for you.

After you've given yourself the permission to cry, yell, scream, and so on, step away from your emotions. One of the more helpful ways to deal with your mother is with emotional distance. No anger, whining, crying, begging, yelling, putting down, just facts. If she on purpose does things to hurt you or make you angry, your best defense or offense is not letting yourself feel hurt or angry.

As much as possible, do what she wants you to do before she asks. This gives her one less thing to be mean about and gives you the upper hand when you ask for what you want.

Pay close attention to the ideas of friends' mothers who are more gentle, steady, and responsible. Get outside information. Much of what you're being told every day is harmful and may be wrong. Instead of just getting mad at her for pointing you wrong, look for sources of better information and remember what they say. Question anything she says about you or about life and compare it with what church leaders, counselors, teachers, healthier adults say. Look at everything in your life because these things don't blow up out of nowhere. They get passed on by generations and you don't want to continue the cycle.

This can be studied, even in books. It can help to understand the family way of acting and choose your own path in life. It may make her even angrier if you don't respond to the usual mind games in the usual way, but it's important to build some inner strength to protect your mind and soul.

Don't be surprised if you get blamed for things you wouldn't even think of doing. If she does them, she expects you to do them whether you would or not. Cruel mothers don't always have that good a hold on what's real and can't tell the difference between when you're behaving well or not. The best thing to do is behave well anyway and try to spend more time with other people so they can see the situation for themselves.

Ask your doctor if you are supposed to take your usual morning medicines. If you have diabetes, ask if you can take insulin or pills for blood sugar before the test. Tell your doctor if you have a history of asthma, kidney or bleeding problems. Special care may be needed if you have one of these health issues.

You may be asked not to take aspirin, including other products that contain aspirin, or doctor-ordered blood thinners for several days before the test. Talk with your doctor about when you can start these medicines again.

Pregnant women need to be careful about doing certain things to avoid harming the baby. If you are or might be pregnant, or if you just had a baby, talk about these details with your doctor so that you can decide on the best thing to do. It is very important to tell your doctor if you are pregnant because an angiogram is needed to find a possible heart artery blockage. This may lead to the need for a treatment called stenting to bring back blood flow to the heart.

Use formula for one to two days after your angiogram if you are breast-feeding until the dye has passed through your body.

Your doctor will figure out what testing you need to do before your angiogram. Make sure you follow your doctor's directions and complete any testing they recommend. You may need to have blood taken or an electrocardiogram done before the angiogram.

Iodine dye is usually used in the heart tube test. Your doctor will need to know if you have such an allergy so you can look at other treatment choices. Other possible dyes can cause a bad reaction in those who are allergic to shellfish.

Most angiograms are planned for the morning hours, so this should not be a huge problem. But it is an important part of getting ready for your angiogram. If your test is scheduled for later in the day, do not eat any food or drink for four to eight hours before the test.

In the hours before your test, especially the twenty-four hours ahead of time, you should avoid alcohol and tobacco products. These can affect your behavior, change test results, and cause other problems during the test. If you are given a calming medicine during the test, this could make stronger the effects of any alcohol in your body.

It is important to tell your doctor about any medicines you are taking, including doctor-ordered medicines, medicines you can buy without a prescription, herbs, and supplements. Bring them in their original bottles. This will help you remember to tell the doctor about the medicines you are on. Remember to also tell the doctor about any medicines you might be allergic to.

Even though the angiogram is a simple test, you will need to come to the hospital ready for a surgery. Some ways to get yourself ready include following your doctor's instructions on what to eat and drink in the twenty-four hours leading up to your test, which may include not eating or drinking anything in the six to eight hours leading up to your test. You should also remove your contact lenses, eyeglasses, hair clips, nail polish, and jewelry before the test. Leave your jewelry at home if possible. Empty your bladder before the test because it can take several hours.

At the hospital you will need to check in and meet with your medical team to talk about exactly what will happen during the test so that you feel prepared. They will let you know about any possible problems or risks.

You will be taken to a room where you can change into a hospital gown before the test begins.

After most angiograms, patients stay at the place for four to six hours after the test. This is so that the staff can watch you and make sure there are no problems after the operation. During this time, try to relax. Do not let yourself worry about the results. Just enjoy taking a break while the doctors are there to watch you.

You may be given a calming medicine during the angiogram test or right before it. This calming medicine will hurt your ability to think clearly and to drive a motor vehicle.

You will need someone to give you a ride home and help you get settled in after your test. Try to find someone you trust who can stay with you for a couple hours, and preferably overnight, after you get home in case you need help with anything. Most medical places will refuse to do an angiogram on you if you do not have a responsible adult with you who has agreed to take you home.

One of the best ways to help your body get better from any kind of test is to get as much rest as possible. This will help your body heal and avoid any possible problems. After the test, you will probably feel a little pain in your groin area. Bed rest will help you avoid moving that area so it can heal the right way.

You should probably plan on staying home for a few days after the test to help you take it easy.

Talk to your doctor about any questions or other worries about the test. Tell them how you are feeling and about any problems you may have run into.

Ask your doctor about the outcome of the test and what the results mean for you moving forward. Are more tests needed? Do you need an operation? Should you change some part of your lifestyle?

Black bears and grizzly bears need different ways to scare them off. Stay alert and avoid coming between a bear and her baby.
A black bear can actually be black, brown or cinnamon colored. They are usually smaller, have pointer ears and don't have a hump.
A grizzly bear is brown, blonde or even slightly silver. They have a hump on their back, have a dish shaped face and rounder ears. Full-grown, they are bigger than black bears.
;
, Their sense of smell is very strong and they are constantly looking for food in the summer and fall months.
, It is a type of pepper spray that creates a 30-foot (9 m) cone of spray. It is only to be used when a bear is running at you to change its direction.
Keep your bear spray within arms reach. Learn where the trigger is in advance.
Pull the trigger when the bear is within 40 feet (12 m) of you.
Never use bear spray as a way to prevent problems before they happen. It is very strong and should not be sprayed on equipment.
, Grizzly and black bears try to avoid this sound. Bear bells are usually too quiet to keep bears away, but human talk will do the trick.
Don't hike alone in bear country. If you don't want to talk, carry a satellite radio and set it to a talk show.
Bears are more likely to come near a single person than a group.
, Bears run up to 35 mph (56 km/h), far faster than humans. They can also follow you up trees or into water.
, The bear will smell you and keep away. If you haven't hidden your food in an airtight, bear-safe container, it could work against you in a bad way.
, Stand your ground and make noise, while avoiding eye contact.
, They may stand on their back legs to get a better look at you, but it's best to be confident and stand your ground.
If a small black bear attacks you, you may be able to fight back.
If a grizzly bear attacks you, curl up in the position babies sleep in before birth. Keep your hands locked behind your back. If the bear sees you are not a danger or dead, it may walk away.
Remember that bear attacks are rare. Most bears prefer to stay away from humans and will only become dangerous if they feel threatened or surprised. Making noise and traveling in groups greatly reduces your chances of having a dangerous meeting with a bear.
words_common_s.coling::22aa3208-6e8c-4005-9386-819f202c:
Pick a time when they are in a good mood. Avoid going up to them right after a hard day at work. Try to figure out their mood by asking, "How was your day?" Choose a time when you will not be stopped or fighting for their attention with other people or problems. Right after dinner or before bed is usually a pretty peaceful and private time.

If you don't get a chance at home, you can also be more creative and talk with them while out on a walk or even while riding in the car. You might say, "Dad, do you want to go on a quick walk? I have some things I'd like to talk with you about." You can always talk with just one parent too and ask them to go to the other one, if needed. This works best if you know your mom, for example, is a bit more easy-going or if you feel closer to her.

Staying honest and clear is just one way to show your grown-up behavior. So, don't tell lies, even small lies. If you've already gone on a date with this guy, you might as well tell them now, if they ask. If you are caught in a lie you will lose any ground that you've gained.

Another part of honesty is your being open to their worries so you can answer them. For example, if they don't trust your boyfriend because they don't know him very well, try to create more opportunities for everyone to get to know each other. This could mean inviting him over for dinner or asking if he can join your family on an outing to the park or to a movie.

Avoid comparing yourself with others if it involves making things bigger than they are. For example, don't tell your parents that your best friend has had a boyfriend for the past two years, unless it is really true. Your parents will sense that you are not being honest and can easily check the facts. They might call the other parents or simply ask around, and then you will be in trouble.

To get what you want, you may have to give a little. If your parents agree to let you have a boyfriend, they will most likely place some conditions on their agreement. If these are promises that you can actually keep, it is best to say yes. You can also bring up give-and-take solutions as a way to bring your parents back to the talking table if they say no at first.

This will create an opening for greater freedom in the future as you gain their trust. The more you show them that you can be trusted and responsible, the more they will be willing to let you make your own choices about dating and relationships.

Many of the conditions will involve your doing well at school. For example, you must keep a certain grade level to have a boyfriend. Or, you need to spend at least one hour each night studying. These are all goals that you should have anyway, so there is no harm in agreeing to them.

It is likely that they will also try to limit your time with your new boyfriend, out of an effort to keep you from getting in over your head. They may ask you to only go out once a week or to stick to a strict time to be home.

They may also want you to see and talk with a health worker. You will need to decide on your own if you are comfortable with this type of give-and-take solution.

Try to control your emotions during your talk. Avoid yelling, crying, complaining, or begging. A temper fit of any kind will make them lose all respect for your position. To stay calm, repeat in your head the word "control" or "calm." Count for five seconds, in your head, before you answer any questions or make any statements you may be sorry for later.

Make sure to watch your tone as well. It is really easy to say nice words with a mean or mocking attitude. For example, "That's great," sounds really different depending on your tone of voice. Pay attention to how you sound when you speak to them.

If you feel more and more upset by the talk, plan a way to blow off some steam after. Picture yourself taking a long run, swimming some laps, or going shopping with friends. This will help you get through the conversation without losing your cool.

Your parents will most likely have quite a bit to say back to you, so make sure to pay close attention to what they are saying. Look into their eyes when they are talking. This will help to show that you are not embarrassed or ashamed to talk about your possible relationship. Nod your head when they make good points and even smile if you really agree with something.

A big part of active listening is asking questions. If they say no to you, answer back by asking, "Why not?" Tell them that you honestly want to understand their way of seeing things in this situation. This will help you to figure out what is bothering them so you can work on it.

If you haven't already talked about it, your parents may want to sit down with you at a later time to talk about their concerns about you having sex. Again, this sex talk could actually be really useful for you. This will be a safe time for you to ask questions or share worries.

If you just can't talk to your parents face-to-face, you may need to write down your feelings and thoughts in a letter. This is also a good idea if you think your parents may have a very strong reaction to your request.

Make sure that your letter is well written and calm. Do not write anything that you will be sorry about later. Instead of saying, "I'm going to have a boyfriend whether you like it or not," you might write, "I really want you to understand where I'm coming from." Be kind and respectful in your words.

It may be helpful to show your letter to a trusted friend or family member for feedback before giving it to your parents. They can help you make sure the letter sounds right and gets your point across clearly.

Trapdoor spiders are around 0.79 in to 1.26 inches (1 to 3 cm) long.That means roughly between the size of your pinky nail and your thumbnail.;
, Trapdoor spiders are black or brown, with thick bodies and legs. Some types have lighter color marks, or they may have a silky covering of hair. Their bodies are divided into two parts: the chest area (containing the head and legs) and the belly.The belly is usually lighter and a slightly different color.
Though they may be hard to see because of its small size, a trapdoor spider will have 6 eyes arranged in 3 groups, while most other spiders have 8 eyes.Trapdoor spiders are relatives of tarantulas, but are less hairy, and have smaller, shinier bodies., The jaws of a trapdoor spider are attached to the front of its head. They move up and down, unlike most other spiders, whose jaws move side to side., Female trapdoor spiders are larger than the males, but you will seldom see females because they rarely leave their holes.Therefore, if you see a trapdoor spider, it is most likely a male. Look for these features that identify male trapdoor spiders:
Short and blunt spinnerets. These make silk, and are located at the tip of the belly.A double point about halfway along their front legs.
A dusty or dull hard covering (a harder area covering much of the chest) that is lightly covered in short stiff hairs.Small parts near the jaws that look like boxing gloves.
, There are many types of trapdoor spiders, each with slightly different physical features.More types of trapdoor spiders are still being found. If you think you have seen a trapdoor spider, look up the exact types that live in your area, so that you know can what kind of exact marks to expect.
, The land spread of trapdoor spiders is uneven and is due to the movement of continents over time. Different types of trapdoor spiders can be found all over the world. Look for trapdoor spiders in:North America: Canada, The United States (southeastern and pacific states, and north to Colorado)
Central America (Guatemala, Mexico, etc.)
Asia (China, Japan, Thailand, etc.)
South Africa and Madagascar
Australia
, Throughout the world, trapdoor spiders like warm places, such as mild forests and deserts. They will dig into the ground in grassy areas, hillsides, and dirt slopes., Trapdoor spiders dig into the ground (about 0.75 inches wide and up to 8 inches deep) and cover their hole with a silky hinged "trapdoor" hidden by sticks, small rocks, and other natural material.Because the holes are hidden, they can be very hard to see.
Larger holes may have more than one trapdoor.
Usually, the hole faces sunlight and will be found near plants.
, Trapdoor spiders are shy, may be active at night, and are rarely seen far from their holes (males may walk around during mating season, however).You might be able to see one, however, when it eats. The spiders will wait in their holes until they sense shaking in the ground caused by insects (including crickets, moths, beetles, and grasshoppers) and other spiders. Then, the spiders will jump out of the trapdoor, grab one of these animals, and pull it back into the hole.

Wipe your knee with a wet cloth and, if needed, a gentle soap. Wash away grease, sweat, and any soap that remains, then dry your knee completely. Making sure your knee is clean and dry will help stop skin problems. You can also shave the area twelve hours before putting on tape if it will be taped many times. This will help reduce pain when the tape is taken off.

Lie with your back raised up or held up and legs stretched out in front of you. Your knees should be completely loose and slightly bent. To help keep your knee bent and loose, place a rolled towel under it.

You will use stiff sports tape to do the actual McConnell method. However, sports tape can be annoying and uncomfortable, so you should first cover your whole knee with a strip of low bother, skin-friendly tape. A breathable white cotton tape that lets air through is a good first layer choice.

Use a marker or pen to gently draw all four sides of your kneecap. This will mark your work area on the first layer. It will be easier to put the sports tape on correctly if you can actually see the kneecap's edges.

Use tape that does not stretch for the McConnell method. Cut a two to three inch strip, which is five to eight centimeters, or enough tape to cover your knee from outer to inner edges. Sports tape with a width of thirty-eight millimeters, which is one and a half inches, is the best size for knee taping.

Put one end of the tape on the outer edge of your kneecap so the tape is straight up and down in the center with the knee. Stick the tape to your skin in a downward direction toward the lower inside corner of your knee, and use your thumb to gently push the kneecap toward the inside of the leg.

While moving the kneecap and putting on the tape, use your fingers to carefully pull the skin on the inside of your leg toward the kneecap. Your goal is to push the kneecap toward the inside of your leg, wrinkle the skin there so it meets the kneecap, and use the tape to hold them tightly together.

Place one edge of the second strip of tape on the outer edge of your knee and, again, make sure it is straight up and down in the center with your kneecap. Stick the tape to your skin in a straight, flat motion from side to side. The tape should make a straight line from the outside of your knee to the inside. Put on one to three more layers of tape until you feel the amount of tightness and support you want.

Make sure you have created skin wrinkles on the inside part of your knee. These wrinkles should run straight up and down, and you should be able to see them through the first layer. Wrinkling of the skin happens when you pull the kneecap inward and stick it to the skin on the inside of the leg.

Wear the tape during movement and exercise as told by your body movement teacher or another medical professional. In general, you should take off the tape within forty-eight hours of putting it on. As strength, range of movement, and balance get better, keep the knee taped for shorter amounts of time during general daily tasks. Work towards taping it only for higher risk activities, like sports.

Hold your kneecap as you slowly peel off the tape to stop making an injury worse. Place your fingers as close as you can to the tape's line of connection, or where it meets your skin. Follow the line with your fingers as you pull the strip of tape to guide it off of your skin. Pulling too fast can cause skin problems or suddenly force the kneecap out of place.

Take off the tape right away if it makes your pain worse. Take the tape off if you feel skin color changes, pins and needles feeling, or swelling after putting on the tape. Tell your body movement teacher or other medical professional about these or any other bad signs that happen from taping. It is best to talk to a medical professional before taping, especially if you have blood flow problems, a knee break, or are sensitive to sports tape in a bad way.
